title.zh: 卷七十七 列傳第二十七: 韋挺 楊纂 劉德威 閻立德 柳亨 崔義玄
title.en: Volume 77 Biographies 27: Wei Ting, Yang Zuan, Liu Dewei, Yan Lide, Liu Heng, Cui Yixuan
title.raw: 卷七十七 列傳第二十七: 韋挺 楊纂 劉德威 閻立德 柳亨 崔義玄 Volume 77 Biographies 27: Wei Ting, Yang Zuan, Liu Dewei, Yan Lide, Liu Heng, Cui Yixuan

sentences.zh: 韋挺 子待價 弟萬石

translations.literal: Wei Ting — his son Daijia — his younger brother Wanshi
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting; his son Daijia; his younger brother Wanshi

sentences.zh: 楊纂 族子弘禮 弘武 武子元亨 元禧 元禕

translations.literal: Yang Zuan — clan nephew Hongli, Hongwu — Wu's sons Yuanheng, Yuanxi, Yuanyi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zuan; his clan nephews Hongli and Hongwu; Hongwu's sons Yuanheng, Yuanxi, and Yuanyi

sentences.zh: 劉德威 子審禮 孫易從 審禮從弟延嗣

translations.literal: Liu Dewei — son Shenli — grandson Yicong — Shenli's younger cousin Yansi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dewei; his son Shenli; his grandson Yicong; Shenli's younger cousin Yansi

sentences.zh: 閻立德 弟立本

translations.literal: Yan Lide — younger brother Liben
translations.idiomatic: Yan Lide; his younger brother Liben

sentences.zh: 柳亨 族子范 兄子奭 亨孫渙 澤

translations.literal: Liu Heng — clan nephew Fan — elder brother's son Shi — Heng's grandsons Huan, Ze
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heng; his clan nephew Fan; his nephew Shi; Heng's grandsons Huan and Ze

sentences.zh: 崔義玄 子神慶

translations.literal: Cui Yixuan — son Shenqing
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yixuan; his son Shenqing

sentences.zh: 韋挺，雍州萬年人，隋民部尚書沖子也。

translations.literal: Wei Ting was a man of Wannian in Yongzhou, son of Chong, Minister of the Household in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting was a native of Wannian in Yongzhou, the son of Wei Chong, who had served as Minister of the Household under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 少與隱太子相善，及高祖平京城，引為隴西公府祭酒。

translations.literal: In youth he was on good terms with the Hidden Crown Prince; when Gaozu pacified the capital city he was brought in as libationer in the Duke of Longxi's household.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was close to the Hidden Crown Prince, and when Gaozu took the capital he was appointed libationer in the household of the Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 武德中，累遷太子左衛驃騎，檢校左率。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he was repeatedly promoted to Left Guards Commissar of the Heir Apparent and acting Left Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude period he rose in succession to Commissar of the Heir Apparent's Left Guards and acting Left Commandant.

sentences.zh: 太子遇之甚厚，宮臣罕與為比。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince treated him very generously; few palace officials could be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince treated him with exceptional favor, and few of the palace officials could rival him in standing.

sentences.zh: 七年，高祖避暑仁智宮，會有上書言事者，稱太子與宮臣潛構異端。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Gaozu went to Renzhi Palace to escape the summer heat; there happened to be one who submitted a memorial on affairs, saying the Crown Prince and palace officials secretly plotted heterodox designs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, while Gaozu was summering at Renzhi Palace, a memorial arrived charging that the Crown Prince and his palace officials were secretly plotting sedition.

sentences.zh: 時慶州刺史楊文干構逆伏誅，辭涉東宮，挺與杜淹、王珪等並坐流於越巂。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Wengan, prefect of Qingzhou, plotted rebellion and was executed upon confession; his testimony implicated the Eastern Palace, and Ting together with Du Yan, Wang Gui, and others were all sentenced to exile in Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Wengan, the prefect of Qingzhou, had plotted rebellion and was put to death; his confession implicated the Eastern Palace, and Ting, together with Du Yan, Wang Gui, and others, were all exiled to Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 及太宗在東宮，征拜主爵郎中。

translations.literal: When Taizong was at the Eastern Palace, he was summoned and appointed Director of Principal Registers.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong held the Eastern Palace, Ting was summoned and appointed Director of Principal Registers.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，王珪數舉之，由是遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan Wang Gui recommended him several times, and thereby he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign, Wang Gui recommended him repeatedly, and he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄授吏部侍郎，轉黃門侍郎，進拜御史大夫，封扶陽縣男。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, transferred to Vice Minister of the Secretariat, advanced to Censor-in-Chief, and enfeoffed as Baron of Fuyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and finally promoted to Censor-in-Chief and enfeoffed as Baron of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗以挺女為齊王祐妃。

translations.literal: Taizong made Ting's daughter consort to Prince Qi, You.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong gave Ting's daughter in marriage to Li You, Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 常與房玄齡、王珪、魏徵、戴胄等俱承顧問，議以政事。

translations.literal: He constantly received consultation together with Fang Xuanling, Wang Gui, Wei Zheng, Dai Zhou, and others, and discussed government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was regularly consulted along with Fang Xuanling, Wang Gui, Wei Zheng, Dai Zhou, and others on matters of state.

sentences.zh: 又與高士廉、令狐德棻等同修《氏族志》，累承賞賚。

translations.literal: He also joined Gao Shilian, Linghu Defen, and others in revising the Genealogical Records, and repeatedly received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He also worked with Gao Shilian, Linghu Defen, and others on revising the Genealogical Records, and received repeated imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂挺曰：「卿之任御史大夫，獨朕意耳，左右大臣無為卿地者，卿勉之哉！」

translations.literal: Taizong once said to Ting: "Your appointment as Censor-in-Chief was solely my wish; none of the ministers on left or right made room for you — strive hard!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once told him, "Your appointment as Censor-in-Chief was entirely my own decision; none of the ministers at court had a hand in it — apply yourself!

sentences.zh: 挺陳謝曰：「臣駑下，不足以辱陛下高位。

translations.literal: Ting declined and said: "Your servant is dull and lowly, not sufficient to disgrace Your Majesty's high post.
translations.idiomatic: Ting declined and said, "Your servant is unworthy and not fit to hold so exalted a post under Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 且臣非勳非舊，而超處籓邸故僚之上，臣願後之，以勸立功者。」

translations.literal: Moreover your servant has neither merit nor old service, yet stands above former colleagues from the princely residence; your servant wishes to be placed behind, to encourage those who establish merit."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have neither distinguished service nor long tenure, yet I stand above former colleagues from the princely household. I ask to be ranked lower, so as to encourage those who earn merit."

sentences.zh: 太宗不許。

translations.literal: Taizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong would not agree.

sentences.zh: 尋改授銀青光祿大夫，行黃門侍郎，兼魏王泰府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, acting Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and concurrently in charge of Prince Tai's household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, acting Vice Minister of the Secretariat, with concurrent duties in Prince Tai's household.

sentences.zh: 時泰有寵，太子承乾多過失，太宗微有廢立之意。

translations.literal: At that time Tai was favored; the Crown Prince Chengqian had many faults, and Taizong vaguely had intent to depose and establish.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Tai was in favor, while the Crown Prince Chengqian had committed many faults, and Taizong was beginning to consider replacing him.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎杜正倫以漏洩禁中語左遷，時挺亦預泰事，太宗謂曰：「朕已罪正倫，不忍更置卿於法。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister Du Zhenglun was demoted for leaking forbidden palace talk; at that time Ting also participated in Tai's affairs. Taizong said: "I have already punished Zhenglun and cannot bear to subject you to the law as well."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Secretariat Du Zhenglun was demoted for leaking palace secrets; since Ting had also been involved in Prince Tai's affairs, Taizong said, "I have already punished Zhenglun, and I cannot bear to subject you to the law as well.

sentences.zh: 特原之。

translations.literal: He specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him a special pardon.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Court Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of Court Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 初，挺為大夫時，馬周為監察御史，挺以周寒士，殊不禮之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ting was Censor-in-Chief, Ma Zhou was an investigating censor; Ting, seeing Zhou was a humble scholar, treated him with no courtesy at all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ting was Censor-in-Chief, Ma Zhou had been an investigating censor; Ting, regarding Zhou as a man of humble birth, had treated him with conspicuous disrespect.

sentences.zh: 至是，周為中書令，太宗嘗復欲用挺在門下，周密陳挺傲狠，非宰相器，遂寢。

translations.literal: By then Zhou was Director of the Secretariat; Taizong once again wished to use Ting in the Secretariat. Zhou in detail stated that Ting was arrogant and fierce and no material for chief minister, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhou had become Director of the Secretariat. When Taizong again considered appointing Ting to the Secretariat, Zhou spoke at length of Ting's arrogance and harshness and declared him unfit for the chief ministership, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十九年，將有事於遼東，擇人運糧，周又奏挺才堪粗使，太宗從之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when there was to be action in Liaodong, men were chosen to transport grain; Zhou again memorialized that Ting's talent was fit for rough service, and Taizong followed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, as preparations began for a campaign in Liaodong, men were chosen to transport supplies. Zhou again memorialized that Ting was fit for rough administrative work, and Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 挺以父在隋為營州總管，有經略高麗遺文。

translations.literal: Ting, because his father in Sui had been regional commander of Yingzhou, had surviving writings on strategy against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's father had served in the Sui as regional commander of Yingzhou and had left writings on strategy against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 因此奏之。

translations.literal: On this account he presented them in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis he presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚悅，謂挺曰：「幽州以北，遼水二千餘里無州縣，軍行資糧無所取給，卿宜為此使。

translations.literal: Taizong was very pleased and said to Ting: "North of Youzhou, for more than two thousand li beyond the Liao River there are no prefectures or counties; marching armies have nowhere from which to draw provisions — you should go on this mission.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was greatly pleased and told him, "North of Youzhou, for more than two thousand li beyond the Liao River there are no prefectures or counties where an army on the march can draw supplies. You are the man for this mission.

sentences.zh: 但得軍用不乏，功不細矣」。

translations.literal: If only military supplies are not lacking, the merit will be no small thing."
translations.idiomatic: If you keep the army supplied, the achievement will be no small one."

sentences.zh: 以人部侍郎崔仁師為副使，任自擇文武官四品十人為子使，以幽、易、平三州驍勇二百人，官馬二百匹為從。

translations.literal: Cui Renshi, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was made deputy commissioner; he was allowed to choose ten civil and military officials of the fourth rank as sub-commissioners, with two hundred fierce men from You, Yi, and Ping prefectures and two hundred government horses as escort.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Renshi, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was appointed his deputy. Ting was permitted to choose ten civil and military officials of the fourth rank as sub-commissioners, and was given two hundred picked troops from You, Yi, and Ping prefectures and two hundred government horses as his escort.

sentences.zh: 詔河北諸州皆取挺節度，許以便宜行事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all Hebei prefectures to obey Ting's direction and permitted him to act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed all prefectures in Hebei to follow Ting's orders and authorized him to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 太宗親解貂裘及中廄馬二匹賜之。

translations.literal: Taizong personally removed his sable fur coat and gave him two horses from the central stables.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong personally removed his sable coat and presented him with two horses from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 挺至幽州，令燕州司馬王安德巡渠通塞。

translations.literal: When Ting reached Youzhou he ordered Yanzhou secretary Wang Ande to inspect whether the canal was open or blocked.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting reached Youzhou, he ordered Wang Ande, the secretary of Yanzhou, to survey the canal and determine whether it was open or obstructed.

sentences.zh: 先出幽州庫物，市木造船，運米而進。

translations.literal: First he took goods from the Youzhou treasury, bought timber to build ships, and advanced grain by transport.
translations.idiomatic: He first drew goods from the Youzhou treasury, purchased timber to build ships, and began shipping grain forward.

sentences.zh: 自桑乾河下至盧思台，去幽州八百里，逢安德還曰：「自此之外，漕渠壅塞。」

translations.literal: From the Sanggan River down to Lusi Terrace was eight hundred li from Youzhou; he met Ande returning, who said: "Beyond this point the transport canal is blocked."
translations.idiomatic: From the Sanggan River down to Lusi Terrace was eight hundred li from Youzhou. When he met Ande on his return, Ande reported, "Beyond this point the transport canal is blocked.

sentences.zh: 挺以北方寒雪，不可更進，遂下米於台側權貯之，待開歲發春，方事轉運，度大兵至，軍糧必足，仍馳以聞。

translations.literal: Ting judged that in the northern cold and snow they could advance no further, so he unloaded the grain beside the terrace for temporary storage, intending when the year opened and spring came to undertake transport — estimating that when the main army arrived army grain would surely suffice — and still hurried a report.
translations.idiomatic: Ting judged that in the northern cold and snow they could advance no farther, so he unloaded the grain beside the terrace for temporary storage, intending to resume transport when spring came. He estimated that by the time the main army arrived the supplies would be adequate, and hurried a report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗不悅，詔挺曰：「兵尚拙速，不貴工遲。

translations.literal: Taizong was displeased and ordered Ting: "In warfare clumsy speed is prized, not skilled delay.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was displeased and sent an edict to Ting: "In warfare, clumsy speed is valued; skilled delay is not.

sentences.zh: 朕欲十九年春大舉，今言二十年運漕，甚無謂也。」

translations.literal: I intend a great campaign in spring of the nineteenth year; now you speak of transporting grain in the twentieth year — it is very meaningless."
translations.idiomatic: I intend a major campaign in the spring of the nineteenth year, yet you speak of transporting supplies in the twentieth — that is absurd.

sentences.zh: 乃遣繁畤令韋懷質往挺所支度軍糧，檢覆渠水。

translations.literal: He then sent Wei Huaizhi, magistrate of Fanshi, to Ting's post to calculate army grain and inspect the canal water.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Wei Huaizhi, magistrate of Fanshi, to Ting's post to assess army provisions and inspect the canal.

sentences.zh: 懷質還奏曰：「挺不先視漕渠，輒集工匠造船，運米即下。

translations.literal: Huaizhi returned and reported: "Ting did not first inspect the transport canal but hastily gathered craftsmen to build ships and sent grain down at once.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhi returned and reported, "Ting did not first inspect the transport canal but hastily gathered craftsmen to build ships and sent the grain downstream at once.

sentences.zh: 至盧思台，方知渠閉，欲進不得，還復水涸，乃便貯之無通平夷之區。

translations.literal: At Lusi Terrace he learned the canal was closed and could not advance; when he returned the water had dried — he simply stored it where there was no level route through.
translations.idiomatic: At Lusi Terrace he discovered the canal was blocked and could go no farther; on the return journey the water had dried up, so he simply stored the grain where there was no level route onward.

sentences.zh: 又挺在幽州，日致飲會，實乖至公。

translations.literal: Moreover at Youzhou Ting daily held drinking gatherings — truly contrary to supreme impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, while at Youzhou, Ting held drinking parties every day — conduct far removed from impartial public service.

sentences.zh: 陛下明年出師，以臣度之，恐未符聖策。」

translations.literal: When Your Majesty campaigns next year, in your servant's judgment it will hardly accord with the sacred plan."
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty campaigns next year, in my judgment the plan will hardly succeed.

sentences.zh: 太宗大怒，令將作少監李道裕代之，仍令治書侍御史唐臨馳傳械挺赴洛陽，依議除名，仍令白衣散從。

translations.literal: Taizong was furious, ordered Chief Director of Palace Construction Li Daoyu to replace him, and still ordered Supervising Secretary Tang Lin to ride posthaste and escort Ting in fetters to Luoyang; by deliberation his name was struck, and he was made to follow as a commoner in white.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was furious. He ordered Li Daoyu, Chief Director of Palace Construction, to replace him, and sent Supervising Secretary Tang Lin posthaste to escort Ting in fetters to Luoyang. By official deliberation Ting's name was struck from the rolls, and he was reduced to following as a commoner in undyed dress.

sentences.zh: 及前軍破蓋牟城，詔挺統兵士鎮蓋牟，示漸用之也。

translations.literal: When the vanguard took Gaemu fortress, an edict ordered Ting to command troops and garrison Gaemu, showing intent to employ him gradually again.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguard captured Gaemu fortress, an edict ordered Ting to command troops and garrison the place, signaling that he might gradually be restored to favor.

sentences.zh: 挺城守去大軍懸遠，與高麗新城鄰接，日夜戰鬥，鼓噪之聲不絕。

translations.literal: Ting in garrison defense was far removed from the main army and adjoined Goguryeo's Xincheng; day and night they fought, and the sound of drums and shouts never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's garrison was far from the main army and bordered on Goguryeo's Xincheng. Fighting went on day and night, and the din of drums and battle cries never ceased.

sentences.zh: 挺不堪其憂，且不平於失職，素與術士公孫常善，乃與常書以敘所懷。

translations.literal: Ting could not bear the distress and was also aggrieved at losing his post; he had long been on good terms with the magician Gongsun Chang, and so wrote Chang to express what was in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ting could not endure the strain and was also bitter over his demotion. He had long been friendly with the magician Gongsun Chang and wrote to him to unburden his feelings.

sentences.zh: 會常以他事被拘，自縊而死，索其囊中，得挺書，論城中危蹙，兼有嘆悵之辭。

translations.literal: When Chang was detained on another matter and hanged himself, they searched his bag and found Ting's letter, discussing the city's peril and also words of lament.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang was detained on another charge and hanged himself, a search of his belongings turned up Ting's letter, describing the city's peril and containing words of complaint and regret.

sentences.zh: 太宗以挺怨望，謫為象州刺史。

translations.literal: Taizong, considering Ting resentful, demoted him to prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, judging that Ting harbored resentment, demoted him to prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲余卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he died, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子待價，初為左千牛備身。

translations.literal: His son Daijia was at first Left Thousand-Bull Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daijia began as a guard of the Left Thousand-Bull unit.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，江夏王道宗得罪，待價即道宗之婿也，緣坐左遷盧龍府果毅。

translations.literal: In Yonghui Prince Jiangxia Daozong incurred guilt; Daijia was Daozong's son-in-law and was implicated, demoted to captain of Lulong militia.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui period, Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong was punished. Daijia, who was married to Daozong's daughter, was implicated and demoted to captain of the Lulong militia.

sentences.zh: 時將軍辛文陵率兵招慰高麗，行至吐護真水，高麗掩其不備，襲擊敗之。

translations.literal: At that time General Xin Wenling led troops to pacify Goguryeo; on reaching the Tuhuzhen River, Goguryeo took them unawares and attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time General Xin Wenling led troops to pacify Goguryeo. When they reached the Tuhuzhen River, the Goguryeo forces caught them unprepared and routed them.

sentences.zh: 待價與中郎將薛仁貴受詔經略東蕃，因率所部救之。

translations.literal: Daijia and Majordomo Xue Rengui received orders to manage the eastern tribes and therefore led their units to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Daijia and Majordomo Xue Rengui received orders to manage the eastern frontier and led their troops to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 文陵苦戰，賊漸退，軍始獲全。

translations.literal: Wenling fought bitterly; the enemy gradually withdrew, and the army at last was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Wenling fought fiercely until the enemy gradually withdrew, and the army was at last saved.

sentences.zh: 待價被重瘡，流矢中其左足，竟不言其功，以足疾免官而歸。

translations.literal: Daijia suffered grave wounds; a stray arrow struck his left foot, yet he never spoke of his merit and was dismissed on account of foot ailment and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Daijia was badly wounded; a stray arrow struck his left foot. He never spoke of his achievements and was dismissed on account of his foot injury, then returned home.

sentences.zh: 後累授蘭州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly appointed prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed in succession to the prefecture of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃屢為邊患，高宗以沛王賢為涼州大都督，以待價為司馬。

translations.literal: At that time Tibet repeatedly became a border trouble; Gaozong made Prince Xian of Pei Grand Governor of Liangzhou, with Daijia as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tibet was a repeated menace on the frontier. Gaozong appointed Prince Xian of Pei Grand Governor of Liangzhou, with Daijia as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 俄又遷蕭州刺史，頻有守禦之功，征拜右武衛將軍，兼檢校右羽林軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was again transferred to prefect of Xiao, had repeated successes in defense, was summoned and appointed General of the Right Martial Guards, and concurrently acting overseer of Right Forest Army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to prefect of Xiao, where he won repeated successes in defense. He was summoned and appointed General of the Right Martial Guards, with concurrent oversight of the Right Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，吐蕃又犯塞，待價復以本官檢校涼州都督，兼知鎮守兵馬事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng Tibet again invaded the frontier; Daijia again with his former title was acting Governor of Liangzhou and concurrently in charge of garrison troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yifeng, Tibet invaded the frontier again. Daijia was again appointed acting Governor of Liangzhou in his former capacity, with charge of garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 俄又征還舊職，復封扶陽侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was again summoned back to his former post and again enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to his former post and again enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，拜吏部尚書，攝司空。

translations.literal: When Wu Zetian held court she appointed him Minister of Personnel and acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian assumed power, she appointed him Minister of Personnel and acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 營高宗山陵，功畢，加金紫光祿大夫，改為天官尚書、同鳳閣鸞台三品，賜物一千段，仍與一子五品。

translations.literal: He supervised construction of Gaozong's mausoleum; when the work was done he was given added Grand Master of the Golden-Purple Glory Light, changed to Minister of the Heavenly Officials and equal Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform, a thousand rolls of goods, and still a fifth-rank post for one son.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised construction of Gaozong's mausoleum. When the work was finished he was promoted to Grand Master of the Golden-Purple Glory Light, made Minister of the Heavenly Officials with equal Third Rank at the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform, granted a thousand rolls of goods, and given a fifth-rank post for one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 待價素無藻鑑之才，自武職而起，居選部，既銓綜無敘，甚為當時所嗤。

translations.literal: Daijia had never had talent for judging men; rising from military office to occupy the selection bureau, his appointments were disorderly and he was much ridiculed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Daijia had never possessed a gift for judging men. Rising from a military career to head the selection bureau, his appointments were chaotic, and he was widely ridiculed at court.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年十月，復為燕然道行軍大總管，以御突厥。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Chuigong he again became Great General on Campaign of the Yanran circuit to repel the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Chuigong he was again appointed Great General on Campaign of the Yanran circuit to repel the Turks.

sentences.zh: 明年春還。

translations.literal: The next spring he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the following spring.

sentences.zh: 六月，拜文昌右相，依舊同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed Right Chancellor of the Literary Gloss Palace, still equal Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed Right Chancellor of the Literary Gloss Palace, retaining equal Third Rank at the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.

sentences.zh: 既累登非據，頗不自安，頻上表辭職，則天每降優制不許之。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly risen beyond his deserts he was quite ill at ease and often memorialized to resign; Wu Zetian each time sent gracious edicts refusing.
translations.idiomatic: Having risen repeatedly beyond his deserts, he grew uneasy and often memorialized to resign, but Wu Zetian each time sent gracious edicts refusing his request.

sentences.zh: 又表請削官秩，回恩贈父，於是贈挺潤州刺史。

translations.literal: He also memorialized asking to cut his own rank and turn the favor to ennoble his father; thereby Ting was posthumously made prefect of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to reduce his own rank and transfer the honor to his father; Ting was accordingly posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，上疏請自效戎旅之用，於是拜安息道行軍大總管，督三十六總管以討吐蕃，進封扶陽郡公。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized asking to offer himself for military service; thereby he was appointed Great General on Campaign of the Anxi circuit, supervising thirty-six commanders to attack Tibet, and advanced to Duke of Fuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized offering himself for military service. He was appointed Great General on Campaign of the Anxi circuit, commanding thirty-six subordinate generals against Tibet, and promoted to Duke of Fuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 軍至寅識迦河，與吐蕃合戰，初勝後敗。

translations.literal: The army reached the Yanshijia River, joined battle with Tibet, was victorious at first then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached the Yanshijia River and engaged the Tibetans. They were victorious at first, then defeated.

sentences.zh: 又屬天寒凍雪，師人多死，糧饋又不支給，乃旋師弓月，頓於高昌。

translations.literal: Moreover it happened to be bitter cold and freezing snow; many in the army died, and provisions could not be supplied — they therefore turned the army at Gongyue and encamped at Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Severe cold and blizzards followed, and many soldiers perished. Provisions ran short, so the army withdrew to Gongyue and encamped at Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 則天大怒，副將閻溫古以逗留伏法，待價坐除名，配流繡州，尋卒。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian was furious; deputy Yan Wengu was executed for delay; Daijia was implicated, his name struck, and he was sentenced to exile in Xiuzhou — soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian was furious. Her deputy Yan Wengu was executed for delay, while Daijia was struck from the rolls and exiled to Xiuzhou, where he soon died.

sentences.zh: 弟萬石，頗有學業，而特善音律。

translations.literal: Younger brother Wanshi was quite learned in scholarship and especially skilled in music and pitch.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wanshi was a man of considerable learning and was especially accomplished in music.

sentences.zh: 上元中，自吏部郎中遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: In Shangyuan he was transferred from Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Vice Minister of Court Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan period he was promoted from Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Vice Minister of Court Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 當時郊廟樂調及宴會雜樂，皆萬石與太史令姚玄辯增損之，時人以為稱職。

translations.literal: At that time music for suburban and temple rites and miscellaneous banquet music were all augmented and reduced by Wanshi and Director of Astronomy Yao Xuanbian; people of the time considered them fit for office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the music for suburban and ancestral rites, as well as the miscellaneous pieces used at banquets, were all revised by Wanshi and the Director of Astronomy Yao Xuanbian, and contemporaries judged them competent in their posts.

sentences.zh: 尋又兼知吏部選事，卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he also concurrently oversaw Ministry of Personnel selection affairs and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took on concurrent charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel and died in office.

sentences.zh: 挺從祖兄子安石，別有傳。

translations.literal: Anshi, son of Ting's second cousin on the father's side, has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi, a son of Ting's second cousin, is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 楊纂，華州華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Zuan was a man of Huayin in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zuan was a native of Huayin in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 祖儉，周東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jian was Eastern Yongzhou prefect in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jian had served as prefect of Eastern Yongzhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父文偉，隋溫州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wenwei was Wenzhou prefect in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenwei had been prefect of Wenzhou under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 纂略涉經史，尤明時務。

translations.literal: Zuan skimmed the classics and histories and was especially clear on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had a working knowledge of the classics and histories and was especially well versed in affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 少與琅邪顏師古、燉煌令狐德棻友善。

translations.literal: In youth he was on friendly terms with Yan Shigu of Langya and Linghu Defen of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was close friends with Yan Shigu of Langya and Linghu Defen of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 大業中，進士舉，授朔方郡司法書佐，坐楊玄感近屬除名，乃家於蒲城。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed judicial secretary of Shuofang commandery, was implicated as kin of Yang Xuangan and struck from the roster, and then made his home in Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye period he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial secretary of Shuofang commandery. Because he was a relative of Yang Xuangan, his name was struck from the rolls, and he settled in Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 義軍渡河，於長春宮謁見。

translations.literal: When the righteous army crossed the river he presented himself at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army crossed the river, he presented himself at Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 累授侍御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed in succession to the post of attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 數上書言事，因被召問，擢為考功郎中。

translations.literal: He memorialized several times on affairs; thereby he was summoned for questioning and promoted to Director of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted several memorials on public affairs, was summoned for questioning, and was promoted to Director of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，長安令，賜爵長安縣男。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was magistrate of Chang'an and enfeoffed as Baron of Chang'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he served as magistrate of Chang'an and was enfeoffed as Baron of Chang'an County.

sentences.zh: 有婦人袁氏妖逆，為人所告，纂究問之，不得其狀。

translations.literal: There was a woman surnamed Yuan guilty of sorcery and heterodoxy who was reported by someone; Zuan investigated and questioned her but could not obtain the facts.
translations.idiomatic: A woman surnamed Yuan was accused of sorcery and sedition. Zuan investigated but could not establish the facts of the case.

sentences.zh: 袁氏後又事發伏誅，太宗以纂為不忠，將殺之。

translations.literal: Yuan later again had her affair exposed and was executed; Taizong considered Zuan disloyal and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan's crimes later came to light and she was executed, Taizong judged Zuan disloyal and was about to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 中書令溫彥博以纂過誤，罪不至死，固諫，乃赦之。

translations.literal: Director Wen Yanbo said Zuan's fault was an error and the crime did not reach death; he remonstrated firmly, and thereby he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Wen Yanbo argued that Zuan's offense was a mistake and did not warrant death. He remonstrated firmly, and Zuan was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times, eventually reaching Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 八年，副特進蕭瑀為河南道巡察大使，與瑀情有不協，屢相表奏，瑀因以獲罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was deputy to Special Palace Attendant Xiao Yu as inspection commissioner on the Henan circuit; he and Yu were not in harmony in feeling and repeatedly memorialized against each other; Yu thereby incurred guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as deputy to Special Palace Attendant Xiao Yu, inspection commissioner on the Henan circuit. He and Xiao Yu were on bad terms and repeatedly memorialized against each other, and Xiao Yu was consequently punished.

sentences.zh: 纂尋拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Zuan was soon appointed Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was soon appointed Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 纂既長於吏道，所在皆有聲績。

translations.literal: Since Zuan was skilled in the way of administration, wherever he was there were reputation and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was skilled in administrative affairs, and wherever he served he left a distinguished record.

sentences.zh: 俄又除吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 前後典選十餘載，銓敘人倫，稱為允當。

translations.literal: For over ten years before and after he presided over selection, assessing and ranking personnel, and was called fair and appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over official selection for more than ten years in all, evaluating and ranking candidates, and was widely regarded as even-handed.

sentences.zh: 然而抑文雅，進酷吏，觀時任數，頗為時論所譏。

translations.literal: Yet he suppressed the refined and literary, advanced harsh officials, watched the times and relied on expedient calculation, and was considerably ridiculed by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he disfavored men of refined learning, promoted harsh officials, and tailored his conduct to the times—a course that drew considerable criticism from his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 後歷太常少卿、雍州別駕，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Prefect of Yongzhou, and was given the honorary title of Silver-Gleam Glory Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Prefect of Yongzhou, and was granted the honorary rank of Silver-Gleam Glory Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 復為尚書左丞，遷太僕卿，檢校雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Again he became Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and held concurrent appointment as Vice Prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and concurrently served as Vice Prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 永徽初卒，贈幽州都督，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: Early in Yonghui he died; posthumously he was given the post of Protector-General of Youzhou, and his posthumous title was Jing (Respectful).
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Yonghui reign. Posthumously he was made Protector-General of Youzhou, with the posthumous epithet Respected (Jing).

sentences.zh: 子守愚，則天時官至雍州長史；

translations.literal: His son Shouyu, in the time of Empress Wu, reached the office of chief secretary of Yongzhou prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouyu, during Empress Wu's reign, rose to chief secretary of Yongzhou;

sentences.zh: 守挹，岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Shouyi was prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi served as prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 族子弘禮。

translations.literal: A clansman, Hongli.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman, Hongli:

sentences.zh: 弘禮，隋尚書令素弟之子也。

translations.literal: Hongli was the son of the younger brother of Yang Su, Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli was a son of the younger brother of Yang Su, who had served as Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 父岳，大業中為萬年令，與素子玄感不協，嘗密上表稱玄感必為亂。

translations.literal: His father Yue, in the Daye era was magistrate of Wannian; he was not in harmony with Su's son Xuangan, and once secretly submitted a memorial saying Xuangan would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue had been magistrate of Wannian during the Daye period. He was on bad terms with Yang Su's son Xuangan and once secretly memorialized the throne that Xuangan would inevitably rebel.

sentences.zh: 及玄感被誅，岳在長安系獄，帝遽使赦之。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was executed, Yue was imprisoned in Chang'an; the emperor hastily sent orders to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was executed, Yue was imprisoned in Chang'an. The emperor immediately sent orders to pardon him.

sentences.zh: 比使至，岳已為留守所殺，弘禮等遂免從坐。

translations.literal: By the time the envoy arrived, Yue had already been killed by the acting governor; Hongli and the others were thereby exempted from guilt by association.
translations.idiomatic: But before the messenger arrived, Yue had already been executed by the acting governor of Chang'an. Hongli and his kin were thus spared punishment as associates.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，以楊素隋代有勳業，詔弘禮襲封清河郡公，拜太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, because Yang Su had merit and achievement in the Sui, an edict ordered Hongli to inherit the enfeoffment as Duke of Qinghe commandery and appointed him palace attendant for miscellaneous affairs of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the transfer of the throne, he recognized Yang Su's distinguished service under the Sui. Hongli was ordered to inherit the title Duke of Qinghe and was appointed palace attendant in charge of miscellaneous affairs for the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，歷兵部員外郎，仍為西河道行軍大總管府長史，三遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he successively served as deputy director in the Ministry of War, again was chief secretary of the headquarters of the Grand General on campaign of the Western River circuit, and was promoted three times to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he served as deputy director in the Ministry of War, then as chief secretary on the staff of the Grand General commanding the Western River circuit army, and was promoted three times to drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗有事遼東，以弘禮有文武材，擢拜兵部侍郎，專典兵機之務。

translations.literal: Taizong had business in Liaodong; because Hongli had both civil and martial talent, he was elevated and appointed Vice Minister of War, exclusively managing military planning affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned in Liaodong, Hongli was promoted to Vice Minister of War for his combined civil and military abilities and was put solely in charge of military planning.

sentences.zh: 弘禮每入參謀議，出則統眾攻戰。

translations.literal: Hongli whenever he entered participated in strategy and deliberation; when he went out he commanded the army in attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli took part in strategic deliberations when at headquarters and led troops in assault when in the field.

sentences.zh: 駐蹕之陣，領馬步二十四軍，出其不意以擊之，所向摧破。

translations.literal: In the encamped formation at Zhuji, he led twenty-four armies of cavalry and infantry, striking them by surprise; wherever he went he crushed and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: At the encamped battle formation at Zhuji, he led twenty-four combined cavalry and infantry armies and struck with surprise attacks, crushing the enemy wherever he advanced.

sentences.zh: 太宗自山下見弘禮所統之眾，人皆盡力，殺獲居多，甚壯之。

translations.literal: Taizong from below the mountain saw the troops Hongli commanded—all exerting themselves to the utmost, with kills and captures in great number—and greatly admired them.
translations.idiomatic: Watching from the foot of the mountain, Taizong saw the troops under Hongli's command fighting with all their strength and amassing many kills and captures. He was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 謂許敬宗等曰：「越公兒郎，故有家風矣。」

translations.literal: He said to Xu Jingzong and the others: "The Duke of Yue's sons indeed carry the family style."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Xu Jingzong and the others, "The sons of the Duke of Yue truly show their family's tradition."

sentences.zh: 時諸宰相併在定州留輔皇太子，唯有褚遂良、許敬宗及弘禮在行在所，掌知機務。

translations.literal: At the time all the chief ministers were left at Dingzhou to assist the Crown Prince; only Chu Suiliang, Xu Jingzong, and Hongli were at the imperial mobile headquarters, managing and knowing urgent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the other chief ministers had all remained at Dingzhou to assist the Crown Prince; only Chu Suiliang, Xu Jingzong, and Hongli accompanied the emperor on campaign and handled urgent state affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of the reign he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，加銀青光祿大夫，尋遷司農卿，兼充昆丘道副大總管，諸道軍將咸受節度。

translations.literal: The next year he was given the honorary title Silver-Gleam Glory Grand Master of the Palace; soon he was transferred to Minister of Public Works, concurrently serving as deputy grand general commanding the Kunqiu circuit; military generals of all circuits all received his command and control.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was granted the honorary rank of Silver-Gleam Glory Grand Master of the Palace. He was soon transferred to Minister of Public Works and concurrently appointed deputy grand general on the Kunqiu circuit, with all regional commanders placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 於是破處月，降處密，殺焉耆王，降馺支部，獲龜茲、于闐王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he broke the Chuyue, caused the Chumi to surrender, killed the king of Yanqi, caused the Sabu tribe to surrender, and captured the kings of Kucha and Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: In these campaigns he defeated the Chuyue, accepted the surrender of the Chumi, killed the king of Yanqi, brought the Sabu tribe to submission, and took captive the kings of Kucha and Khotan.

sentences.zh: 凱旋，未及行賞，太宗晏駕。

translations.literal: Returning in triumph, before rewards were carried out, Taizong passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He returned in triumph, but before rewards could be distributed, Emperor Taizong died.

sentences.zh: 弘禮頗忤大臣之旨，由是出為涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Hongli considerably went against the intent of the chief ministers; thereby he was sent out as prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli had seriously offended the chief ministers and was consequently transferred out to serve as prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，論昆丘之功，改授勝州都督。

translations.literal: Early in Yonghui, evaluating the achievements of the Kunqiu campaign, he was reassigned as Protector-General of Shengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui reign, in recognition of his service on the Kunqiu campaign, he was reassigned as Protector-General of Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太府卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 四年卒，贈蘭州都督，謚曰質。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died; posthumously he was given Protector-General of Lanzhou; his posthumous title was Zhi (Integrity).
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the reign. Posthumously he was made Protector-General of Lanzhou, with the posthumous epithet Integrity (Zhi).

sentences.zh: 弟弘武。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Hongwu:

sentences.zh: 弘武少修謹，武德初，拜左千牛備身。

translations.literal: Hongwu from youth was cultivated and careful; early in Wude he was appointed attendant in the Left Office of Palace Horse Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu was from youth disciplined and conscientious. Early in the Wude reign he was appointed attendant of the Left Office of the Palace Horse Guard.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In Yonghui he was a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign he served as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 孝敬初，為皇太子精擇僚采，以弘武為中舍人。

translations.literal: Early in the Xiaojing era, in carefully selecting staff for the Crown Prince, Hongwu was made palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince's household was being carefully staffed early in the Xiaojing era, Hongwu was appointed palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，將有事於東嶽，弘武自荊州司馬擢拜司戎少常伯。

translations.literal: In the Linde era, when there were to be affairs at the Eastern Peak, Hongwu was elevated from chief secretary of Jingzhou to Lesser Director on the Left of the Guard of the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: During the Linde era, as preparations were underway for ceremonies at Mount Tai, Hongwu was promoted from secretary-general of Jingzhou to Lesser Director on the Left of the Guard of the Realm.

sentences.zh: 從駕還，高宗特令弘武補授吏部選人五品已上官，由是漸見親委。

translations.literal: Returning from accompanying the imperial procession, Gaozong specially ordered Hongwu to supplement and appoint officials of fifth rank and above from among candidates of the Ministry of Personnel; thereby he gradually came to be seen as trusted and entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: On the return from the imperial tour, Gaozong specially authorized Hongwu to appoint fifth-rank officials and above from among personnel candidates, and from this he gradually gained the emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 後母榮國夫人楊氏，以與弘武同宗，又稱薦之，俄遷西台侍郎。

translations.literal: His stepmother Lady Yang of the State of Glory, because she shared the same clan with Hongwu, also praised and recommended him; soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Western Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother, Lady Yang of the State of Glory, who was of the same Yang clan, also recommended him, and he was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Western Terrace.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年，與戴至德、李安期等同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng he was made Third Rank of the Eastern and Western Terraces together with Dai Zhide and Li Anqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianfeng he was made a Third-Rank official of the combined Eastern and Western Terraces, serving alongside Dai Zhide and Li Anqi.

sentences.zh: 及在政事，頗以清簡見稱。

translations.literal: When he was in governance, he was rather praised for being pure and simple.
translations.idiomatic: In office he won praise for his integrity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，卒於官，贈汴州刺史，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang he died in office; posthumously he was given Prefect of Bianzhou; his posthumous title was Gong (Respectful).
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the first year of Zongzhang. Posthumously he was made prefect of Bianzhou, with the posthumous epithet Respectful (Gong).

sentences.zh: 子元亨，則天時為司府少卿；

translations.literal: His son Yuanheng, in Empress Wu's time was Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanheng, during Empress Wu's reign, served as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury;

sentences.zh: 元禧，尚食奉御。

translations.literal: Yuanxi was commissioner of imperial provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi served as commissioner of imperial provisions.

sentences.zh: 元禧頗有醫術，為則天所任。

translations.literal: Yuanxi had considerable medical skill and was entrusted by Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi was skilled in medicine and enjoyed Empress Wu's trust.

sentences.zh: 嘗忤張易之之意，易之密奏元禧是楊素兄弟之後，素父子在隋有逆節，子孫不合供奉。

translations.literal: Once he went against Zhang Yizhi's wish; Yizhi secretly memorialized that Yuanxi was a descendant of Yang Su's brothers, and that Su, father and son, had had treacherous conduct in the Sui—their descendants were not fit to serve in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After he once offended Zhang Yizhi, Yizhi secretly memorialized that Yuanxi was a descendant of Yang Su's kin, that Yang Su and his son had committed treason under the Sui, and that their descendants were unfit to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 則天乃下制曰：「隋尚書令楊素，昔在本朝，早荷殊遇。

translations.literal: Empress Wu then issued an edict saying: "Yang Su, Sui Director of the Department of State Affairs, in former times in our dynasty early received extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu then issued an edict: "Yang Su, who had served as Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Sui, was once greatly favored in our own dynasty.

sentences.zh: 稟凶邪之德，懷諂佞之才，惑亂君上，離間骨肉。

translations.literal: He bore a vicious and evil virtue, harbored flattery and sycophancy as talent, confused and disturbed the ruler above, and estranged flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature vicious and corrupt, skilled in flattery and sycophancy; he misled the sovereign and set kin against kin.

sentences.zh: 搖動冢嫡，寧唯掘蠱之禍？

translations.literal: He stirred up the legitimate heir—was the calamity of the uprooting-sorcery affair the only one?
translations.idiomatic: He undermined the legitimate heir—the uprooting-sorcery scandal was hardly his only crime.

sentences.zh: 誘扇後主，卒成請蹯之釁。

translations.literal: He enticed and incited the later sovereign, and in the end completed the provocation of requesting a leg.
translations.idiomatic: He goaded the last Sui emperor until their quarrel culminated in the notorious affair of 'requesting the emperor's leg.'

sentences.zh: 隋室喪亡，蓋惟多僻，究其萌兆，實此之由。

translations.literal: The Sui house's loss and ruin—perhaps it had many perverse ways; tracing its first sprout and omen, truly this was the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of the Sui was brought on by many depravities, but tracing the first seeds of disaster leads back to him.

sentences.zh: 生為不忠之人，死為不義之鬼，身雖倖免，子竟族誅。

translations.literal: Alive he was an unfaithful man; dead he became an unrighteous ghost; though his person narrowly escaped, his sons in the end were executed by clan extermination.
translations.idiomatic: He lived as a traitor and died a faithless spirit. Though he himself narrowly escaped punishment, his sons were ultimately wiped out to the last clan.

sentences.zh: 斯則奸逆之謀，是其庭訓；

translations.literal: Thus then—treacherous and rebellious schemes were his household instruction;
translations.idiomatic: Treason and rebellion were the lessons taught in his household;

sentences.zh: 險薄之行，遂成門風。

translations.literal: Treacherous and shallow conduct thereby became the family style.
translations.idiomatic: Cunning and depravity became the family way.

sentences.zh: 刑戮雖加，枝胤仍在，豈可復肩隨近侍，齒跡朝行？

translations.literal: Though punishments by execution were applied, branch descendants still remain—how can they again shoulder-along close attendants and rank-alongside the court procession?
translations.idiomatic: Even after executions, his line survives. How can his descendants again walk among imperial attendants and take their place in the court ranks?

sentences.zh: 朕接統百王，恭臨四海，上嘉賢佐，下捍賊臣，常欲從容於萬機之餘，褒貶於千載之外，況年代未遠，耳目所存者乎？

translations.literal: I have received and continued a hundred kings, respectfully facing the four seas; above I praise worthy assistants, below I repel treacherous ministers; I always wish, at leisure beyond the myriad affairs of state, to praise and blame a thousand years hence—how much more when the years are not distant and what eyes and ears preserve still exists?
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the throne from a hundred sage rulers and ruling over the realm, I honor worthy ministers and cast out traitors. I have long wished, even amid the press of governance, to render judgment for posterity—and all the more when the events are recent and still fresh in living memory.

sentences.zh: 其楊素及兄弟子孫，並不得令任京官及侍衛。」

translations.literal: Yang Su and his brothers' descendants—none may be allowed to hold capital offices or palace guard service."
translations.idiomatic: None of Yang Su's brothers and their descendants shall be permitted to hold offices in the capital or serve as imperial guards."

sentences.zh: 於是左貶元亨為睦州刺史，元禧為資州長史，元禧弟緱氏令元禕為梓州司馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanheng was demoted left to prefect of Muzhou, Yuanxi to chief secretary of Zizhou, and Yuanxi's younger brother Yuanyi, magistrate of Gou, to secretary of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Yuanheng was demoted to prefect of Muzhou, Yuanxi to chief secretary of Zizhou, and Yuanxi's younger brother Yuanyi, formerly magistrate of Gou County, to secretary of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 張易之誅後，元亨等皆復任京職，元亨至齊州刺史，元禧台州刺史，元禕宣州刺史。

translations.literal: After Zhang Yizhi was executed, Yuanheng and the others all again held capital offices; Yuanheng reached Prefect of Qizhou, Yuanxi Prefect of Taizhou, Yuanyi Prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yizhi's execution, Yuanheng and the others were all restored to office; Yuanheng eventually became prefect of Qizhou, Yuanxi prefect of Taizhou, and Yuanyi prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉德威

translations.literal: Liu Dewei
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dewei

sentences.zh: 劉德威，徐州彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Dewei was a man of Pengcheng in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dewei was a native of Pengcheng in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父子將，隋毗陵郡通守。

translations.literal: His father Zijiang was Sui thoroughfare administrator of Piling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zijiang had served as acting governor of Piling commandery under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 德威姿貌魁偉，頗以干略見稱。

translations.literal: Dewei's bearing and appearance were towering and grand; he was rather praised for practical strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei was a man of imposing stature and was widely noted for his practical ability and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 大業末，從左光祿大夫裴仁基討賊淮左，手斬賊帥李青珪，傳首於行在所。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he followed Left Glory Grand Master of the Palace Pei Renji in punishing bandits on the left of the Huai River; with his own hand he beheaded the bandit chief Li Qinggui and sent the head to the mobile imperial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he followed Left Glory Grand Master of the Palace Pei Renji in campaigning against bandits along the lower Huai. He personally beheaded the bandit leader Li Qinggui and sent the head to the emperor's field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後與仁基同歸李密，密素聞其名，與麾下兵，令於懷州鎮守。

translations.literal: Later he together with Renji submitted to Li Mi; Mi had long heard his name, gave him troops under his banner, and ordered him to guard and hold at Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Renji in submitting to Li Mi. Mi, who had long heard of his reputation, gave him a command and posted him to hold Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，密與王世充戰敗入朝，德威亦率所部隨密歸款。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, Mi was defeated by Wang Shichong and entered court; Dewei also led his command following Mi in submitting allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Li Mi was defeated by Wang Shichong and surrendered to the Tang court. Dewei led his troops in following Mi to submit.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，授左武候將軍，封滕縣公。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised this; he was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Teng County.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu commended him, appointing him General of the Left Martial Guard and enfeoffing him as Duke of Teng County.

sentences.zh: 及劉武周南侵，詔德威統兵擊之，又判并州總管府司馬。

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou invaded southward, an edict ordered Dewei to command troops to strike him, and he also served concurrently as secretary of the Bingzhou supreme headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou invaded from the north, Dewei was ordered to command troops against him and was concurrently appointed secretary of the Bingzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 俄而裴寂失律於介州，齊王元吉棄并州還朝，留德威總知留府事。

translations.literal: Soon Pei Ji lost discipline at Jiezhou; Prince of Qi Yuanji abandoned Bingzhou and returned to court, leaving Dewei in overall charge of remaining headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Pei Ji suffered defeat at Jiezhou. Prince of Qi Li Yuanji abandoned Bingzhou and returned to court, leaving Dewei in overall charge of the headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 元吉才出，武周已至城下，百姓相率投賊。

translations.literal: Yuanji had just gone out when Wuzhou had already reached below the city walls; common people one after another went over to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji had barely departed when Wuzhou's forces were already at the city walls, and the populace surrendered to the enemy in droves.

sentences.zh: 武周獲德威，令率其本兵往浩州招慰。

translations.literal: Wuzhou captured Dewei and ordered him to lead his original troops to Haozhou to summon and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou captured Dewei and ordered him to lead his former troops to Haozhou to win over the local population.

sentences.zh: 德威自拔歸朝，高祖親勞問之，兼陳賊中虛實及晉、絳諸部利害，高祖皆嘉納之。

translations.literal: Dewei on his own freed himself and returned to court; Gaozu personally comforted and questioned him; he also set forth the rebels' reality and the advantages and harms of Jin and Jiang prefectures—all of which Gaozu praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei escaped and returned to the Tang court. Gaozu personally received him and questioned him at length. Dewei reported on conditions among the rebels and on the strategic situation in Jin and Jiang, and Gaozu welcomed all his counsel.

sentences.zh: 改封彭城縣公。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Pengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Pengcheng County.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校大理少卿。

translations.literal: Before long he held concurrent appointment as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed acting Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 從擒建德，平世充，皆有功，轉刑部侍郎，加散騎常侍，妻以平壽縣主。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Jiande and pacification of Shichong, he had merit in both; he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, given the added title Palace Attendant, and given in marriage Ping Shou County Princess.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the captures of Dou Jiande and Wang Shichong. He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, given the additional title of Palace Attendant, and married to the Princess of Pingshou County.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷大理、太僕二卿，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he successively served as Minister of Judicial Review and Minister of the Imperial Stud, and was given the honorary title Golden-Gleam Glory Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he served in succession as Minister of Judicial Review and Minister of the Imperial Stud, and was granted the honorary rank of Golden-Gleam Glory Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 俄出為綿州刺史，以廉平著稱，百姓為之立碑。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as prefect of Mianzhou; for integrity and fairness he was famed, and the common people erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to serve as prefect of Mianzhou, where his integrity and fairness won renown and the people erected a monument in his honor.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Soon he held concurrent appointment as chief secretary of the Great Protectorate headquarters of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting chief secretary of the Yizhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復授大理卿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again given the post of Minister of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the reign he was again appointed Minister of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗問之曰：「近來刑網稍密，其過安在？」

translations.literal: Taizong once asked him, saying: "Recently the penal net has become somewhat tight—where does the fault lie?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once asked him, "Punishments have grown noticeably harsher of late. Where does the fault lie?"

sentences.zh: 德威奏言：「誠在主上，不由臣下。

translations.literal: Dewei memorialized, saying: "Truly it lies in the lord above—it is not from ministers below.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei replied, "Truly the cause lies with Your Majesty, not with your officials.

sentences.zh: 人主好寬則寬，好急則急，律文失入減三等，失出減五等。

translations.literal: If the ruler favors leniency then there is leniency; if he favors severity then there is severity. In the law's text, erroneous conviction reduces three degrees; erroneous acquittal reduces five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler favors leniency, officials are lenient; when he favors severity, they are severe. The law stipulates that an erroneous conviction reduces the official's penalty by three degrees, an erroneous acquittal by five.

sentences.zh: 今則反是，失入則無辜，失出便獲大罪。

translations.literal: Now it is the opposite: erroneous conviction then he is innocent; erroneous acquittal then he incurs great guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is the reverse: a judge who wrongly convicts goes unpunished, while one who wrongly acquits faces heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 所以吏各自愛，競執深文，非有教使之然，畏罪之所致耳。

translations.literal: Therefore officials each protect themselves, competing to apply harsh legal wording—it is not that there is instruction making it so; it is fear of guilt that brings it about.
translations.idiomatic: That is why officials look out for themselves and compete in applying the harshest interpretation of the law—not because anyone orders them to, but because they fear punishment.

sentences.zh: 陛下但舍所急，則『寧失不經』復行於今日矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only set aside what is urgent, and then "better to err in acquittal than in conviction" will again be practiced today."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would only set aside this emphasis on severity, the principle that it is better to err in acquittal than in conviction would prevail again."

sentences.zh: 太宗深然之。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 數歲，遷刑部尚書，兼檢校雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Minister of Justice and concurrently held appointment as Vice Prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed Minister of Justice and concurrently served as Vice Prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年，馳驛往濟州推齊王祐還，至濮州，聞祐殺長史權萬紀，德威入據濟州，遣使以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he traveled by post-horse relay to Jizhou to urge Prince of Qi You to return; reaching Puzhou, he heard You had killed chief secretary Quan Wanji; Dewei entered and held Jizhou, and sent a messenger to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he rode post-horses to Jizhou to escort Prince of Qi Li You back to court. Reaching Puzhou, he learned that Li You had killed his chief secretary Quan Wanji. Dewei entered and secured Jizhou, then dispatched a messenger to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔德威便發河南兵馬，以申經略，會遭母憂而罷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dewei immediately to mobilize Henan military forces to carry out strategy; he happened to encounter mourning for his mother and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to mobilize Henan troops immediately to take control of the situation, but he was compelled to withdraw when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起為遂州刺史，三遷同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was recalled to serve as prefect of Suizhou; he was promoted three times to prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was recalled from mourning to serve as prefect of Suizhou, and was later promoted three times, eventually becoming prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he died, age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Yonghui reign, at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書、幽州都督，謚曰襄，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Minister of Rites and Protector-General of Youzhou; his posthumous title was Xiang; he was buried by accompaniment at Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Minister of Rites and Protector-General of Youzhou, with the posthumous epithet Xiang (Assisting). He was buried near Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 德威閨門友穆，接物寬平，所得財貨，多以分贍宗親。

translations.literal: Dewei's inner gates were friendly and harmonious; in receiving people he was broad and fair; goods obtained he largely used to divide and support clan kin.
translations.idiomatic: Within his household Dewei was cordial and harmonious; in dealing with others he was generous and even-handed. Much of what he acquired he distributed among his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 子審禮襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shenli inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenli inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 審禮，少喪母，為祖母元氏所養。

translations.literal: Shenli, in youth lost his mother and was reared by his grandmother of the Yuan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenli lost his mother at a young age and was raised by his grandmother, née Yuan.

sentences.zh: 隋末，德威從裴仁基討擊，道路不通。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, Dewei followed Pei Renji in punitive attacks; the roads were not passable.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, Dewei joined Pei Renji on campaign, but communications were cut off.

sentences.zh: 審禮年未弱冠，自鄉里負載元氏，渡江避亂。

translations.literal: Shenli's years had not yet reached weak-cap; from his home village he carried Yuan on his back, crossed the river to avoid disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shenli was still in his teens. He carried his grandmother Yuan on his back from their home village, crossed the Yangzi, and fled the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 及天下定，始西入長安。

translations.literal: When the realm was settled, he first entered Chang'an from the west.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the realm was pacified did they travel west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 元氏若有疾，審禮必親嘗湯藥，元氏顧謂孫曰：「我兒孝順，貫徹幽微，吾一顧念，宿疾頓輕。」

translations.literal: Whenever Yuan had illness, Shenli always personally tasted the decoction; Yuan turned and said to her grandson: "My son is filially obedient—it penetrates through to the subtle; at one thought from me, my old illness suddenly lightens."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yuan fell ill, Shenli always tasted her medicine himself. Yuan would turn to her grandson and say, "This child is truly filial—his devotion reaches into the smallest details. The moment I think of him, my chronic ailments ease."

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，歷左驍衛郎將。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he successively served as Commander of the Left Martial Roaming Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he served as commander in the Left Martial Roaming Guard.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂去職。

translations.literal: Upon encountering mourning for his father he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 及葬，跣足隨車，流血灑地，行路稱之。

translations.literal: At the burial, barefoot he followed the carriage; blood sprinkled the ground; travelers on the road praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral he walked barefoot behind the coffin, the blood from his torn feet staining the ground—a display of grief that passersby praised.

sentences.zh: 服闋當襲爵，累表讓弟，朝議不許。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he was to inherit the enfeoffment; repeatedly he memorialized yielding to his younger brother; court deliberation did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was due to inherit the title, but he repeatedly petitioned to yield it to his younger brother. The court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，累遷將作大匠，兼檢校燕然都護，襲封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Palace Construction, concurrently acting as Protector-General of Yanran, and inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui he rose to Grand Master of Palace Construction and acting Protector-General of Yanran, and inherited the title Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 審禮父歿雖久，猶悲慕不已，每見父時僚舊，必嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: Though Shenli's father's death had been long, still he grieved and yearned unceasingly; whenever he saw his father's former colleagues, he would sob and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Long after his father's death, Shenli still mourned him deeply. Whenever he met his father's former colleagues, he would weep aloud.

sentences.zh: 母鄭氏早亡，事繼母平壽縣主，稍疾輒憂懼形於容色，終夕不寐。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Zheng had died early; he served his stepmother the Princess of Pingshou; at the slightest illness he would show worry and fear in his countenance and not sleep the whole night.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zheng, had died young. He cared for his stepmother, the Princess of Pingshou County; at the slightest sign of illness his face showed fear and he would go without sleep all night.

sentences.zh: 撫繼母男延景，友愛甚篤。

translations.literal: He reared his stepmother's son Yanjing with friendship and love very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his stepmother's son Yanjing with deep affection.

sentences.zh: 所得祿俸，皆送母處，以資延景之費；

translations.literal: The salary he received he sent entirely to his mother's place, to supply Yanjing's expenses;
translations.idiomatic: He sent all his salary to his stepmother to cover Yanjing's expenses;

sentences.zh: 而審禮妻子處飢寒，晏然未嘗介意。

translations.literal: Yet Shenli's wife and children dwelt in hunger and cold, calmly and never once minded it.
translations.idiomatic: while Shenli's own wife and children lived in hunger and cold—yet he remained untroubled and never complained.

sentences.zh: 再從同居，家無異爨，合門二百餘口，人無間言。

translations.literal: Second and third cousins lived together; the household had no separate cooking; the whole clan exceeded two hundred mouths, and among the people there was no discordant speech.
translations.idiomatic: Cousins of the second and third degree lived together under one roof with a single kitchen. More than two hundred people shared the household, and no one spoke ill of one another.

sentences.zh: 稍遷工部尚書，兼檢校左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Minister of Works and concurrently acting Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Minister of Works and acting Grand General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，吐蕃寇涼州，命審禮為行軍總管，與中書令李敬玄合勢討擊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, Tibet raided Liang prefecture; Shenli was ordered as Campaign Commander, joining forces with Chief Minister Li Jingxuan to attack and strike.
translations.idiomatic: In 677, when Tibet invaded Liangzhou, Shenli was appointed campaign commander and joined Chief Minister Li Jingxuan in a joint offensive.

sentences.zh: 遇賊於青海，敬玄後期不至，審禮事敗，為賊所執。

translations.literal: They encountered the bandits at Qinghai; Jingxuan was late and did not arrive; Shenli's affair failed and he was seized by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They met the enemy at Qinghai Lake. Jingxuan failed to arrive on time, the campaign collapsed, and Shenli was captured.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，卒於蕃中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong he died in the land of the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In 681 he died in Tibetan captivity.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書，謚曰僖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works; posthumous title Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Works with the posthumous name Xi.

sentences.zh: 延景，官至陝州刺史，睿宗初，以後父追贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Yanjing reached the office of Prefect of Shan prefecture; at the beginning of Ruizong's reign, as the empress's father he was posthumously granted Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing rose to prefect of Shanzhou. At the start of Emperor Ruizong's reign he was posthumously made Right Vice Minister of State as the empress's father.

sentences.zh: 審禮子易從，歷位岐州司兵參軍。

translations.literal: Shenli's son Yicong successively held the post of Army Registrar of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shenli's son Yicong served as army registrar in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 審禮之沒吐蕃，詔許易從入蕃省之。

translations.literal: When Shenli perished in Tibet, an edict permitted Yicong to enter Tibet to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenli was lost in Tibet, the court authorized Yicong to travel there to see him.

sentences.zh: 及審禮卒，易從號哭，晝夜不止，毀瘠過禮。

translations.literal: When Shenli died, Yicong wailed and cried day and night without cease, his emaciation exceeding the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenli died, Yicong wailed day and night without stopping, wasting away beyond what mourning rites required.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃哀其志行，還其父屍柩，易從徒跣萬里，扶護歸彭城，為朝野之所嗟賞。

translations.literal: Tibet pitied his resolve and conduct and returned his father's corpse and coffin; Yicong went barefoot ten thousand li, supporting and escorting it back to Pengcheng, and court and countryside alike sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his devotion, the Tibetans returned his father's coffin. Yicong walked barefoot three thousand miles, escorting it home to Pengcheng—a feat admired throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 後歷彭州長史、任城男。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Chief Administrator of Peng prefecture and Baron of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief administrator of Pengzhou and was enfeoffed as Baron of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 永昌中，坐為徐敬貞所誣構遇害。

translations.literal: In the Yongchang era he was implicated and harmed by Xu Jingzhen's false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongchang he was framed by Xu Jingzhen and put to death.

sentences.zh: 易從在官仁恕，及將刑，人吏無遠近奔走，競解衣相率造功德，以為長史祈福，州人從之者十餘萬。

translations.literal: Yicong in office was benevolent and forgiving; when he was about to be executed, officials and commoners from near and far ran, competing to remove their garments and in groups going to perform meritorious deeds to pray for the chief administrator's blessing; more than a hundred thousand people of the prefecture followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yicong was known for his kindness in office. When he was about to be executed, officials and commoners from far and near rushed to strip off their clothes and perform acts of merit on his behalf; more than a hundred thousand people in the prefecture joined them.

sentences.zh: 其為人所愛如此。

translations.literal: He was loved by people to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the affection in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 易從子升，開元中，為中書舍人、太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Yicong's son Sheng, in the Kaiyuan era, served as Secretariat Drafter and Right Censor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yicong's son Sheng served under Emperor Xuanzong as a secretariat drafter and right censor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 審禮從父弟延嗣，文明年為潤州司馬，屬徐敬業作亂，率眾攻潤州，延嗣與刺史李思文固守不降。

translations.literal: Shenli's paternal cousin Yansi, in the Wensheng era was Prefectural Secretary of Run prefecture; when Xu Jingye raised rebellion he led troops to attack Run prefecture; Yansi and Prefect Li Siwen firmly defended and did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shenli's cousin Yansi was prefectural secretary of Runzhou during the Wensheng era. When Xu Jingye rebelled and besieged the city, Yansi and Prefect Li Siwen held out and refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，敬業執延嗣，邀之令降，辭曰：「延嗣世蒙國恩，當思效命，州城不守，多負朝廷。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; Jingye seized Yansi and invited him to order surrender; he replied: "Yansi for generations received the state's grace and ought to think of repaying with his life; the prefectural city was not held—greatly failing the court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell. Jingye captured Yansi and pressed him to submit. Yansi replied, "My family has received the state's favor for generations. I should have given my life in its service. I failed to hold the city and have already wronged the court.

sentences.zh: 終不能苟免偷生，以累宗族，豈以一身之故，為千載之辱？

translations.literal: In the end I cannot by chance escape and steal life, thereby burdening my clan—how could I for the sake of one body make a disgrace for a thousand years?
translations.idiomatic: I could never save myself at the cost of disgracing my clan for generations. How could I preserve my own life and bring eternal shame on my family?

sentences.zh: 今日之事，得死為幸。」

translations.literal: Today's affair—obtaining death is fortune."
translations.idiomatic: As for what faces me today, to die is my good fortune."

sentences.zh: 敬業大怒，將斬之，其黨魏思溫救之獲免，乃囚之於江都獄。

translations.literal: Jingye was greatly enraged and was about to behead him; his follower Wei Siwen rescued him and he was spared, and then he was imprisoned in the Jiangdu jail.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye flew into a rage and was about to execute him, but his follower Wei Siwen intervened and saved him. Yansi was imprisoned in the jail at Jiangdu instead.
