sentences.zh: 俄而賊敗，竟以裴炎近親，不得敘功，遷為梓州長史，再轉汾州刺史卒。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels were defeated; in the end because he was a close kinsman of Pei Yan he could not have merit recorded; he was moved to Chief Administrator of Zi prefecture, then again transferred to Prefect of Fen prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were soon defeated, he received no reward because of his kinship to Pei Yan. He was transferred to chief administrator of Zizhou, then prefect of Fenzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 宗族至刺史者二十餘人。

translations.literal: In the clan those reaching prefect reached more than twenty men.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty men of the clan rose to the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 閻立德

translations.literal: Yan Lide
translations.idiomatic: Yan Lide

sentences.zh: 閻立德，雍州萬年人，隋殿內少監毗之子也。

translations.literal: Yan Lide, a man of Wannian in Yong prefecture, was the son of Pi, Palace Attendant of the Inner Hall in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Lide was a native of Wannian in Yongzhou and the son of Pi, who had served as Sui Palace Attendant of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 其先自馬邑徙關中。

translations.literal: His ancestors had moved from Mayi to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His family had migrated from Mayi to the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 毗初以工藝知名，立德與弟立本，早傳家業。

translations.literal: Pi at first was famed for craftsmanship; Lide and his younger brother Liben early transmitted the family profession.
translations.idiomatic: Pi had first won renown as a craftsman; Lide and his younger brother Liben inherited the family trade from an early age.

sentences.zh: 武德中，累除尚衣奉御，立德所造袞冕大裘等六服並腰輿傘扇，咸依典式，時人稱之。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he was repeatedly appointed Master of Imperial Robes; the six garments Lide made, including the sacrificial robes and great fur cloak, together with waist carriages, parasols, and fans, all followed canonical forms, and people of the time praised them.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude he was repeatedly appointed Master of Imperial Robes. The six ceremonial garments he produced—including the sacrificial robes and great fur cloak—as well as imperial litters, parasols, and fans all conformed to canonical specifications, and contemporaries praised his work.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷遷將作少匠，封太安縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was successively promoted to Vice Master of Palace Construction and enfeoffed Baron of Tai'an county.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenguan reign he rose to Vice Master of Palace Construction and was enfeoffed Baron of Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，立德以營山陵功，擢為將作大匠。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Lide because of the merit of constructing the imperial tomb was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death, Lide was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Construction for overseeing the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年，文德皇后崩，又令攝司空，營昭陵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan Empress Wende died, and again he was ordered to act as Minister of Works and construct Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In 636, when Empress Wende died, he was again ordered to serve as acting Minister of Works and build Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 坐怠慢解職。

translations.literal: For negligence he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for negligence.

sentences.zh: 俄起為博州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised up as Prefect of Bo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復為將作大匠。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he again became Grand Master of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: In 639 he returned to the post of Grand Master of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 十八年，從征高麗，及師旅至遼澤，東西二百餘里泥淖，人馬不通。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he followed the expedition against Goguryeo; when the army reached Liaomarsh, for two hundred-odd li east and west there was mud and slough, and men and horses could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: In 644 he accompanied the campaign against Goguryeo. When the army reached the Liaodong marshes, two hundred li of mud blocked the way and neither men nor horses could pass.

sentences.zh: 立德填道造橋，兵無留礙。

translations.literal: Lide filled the road and built bridges; the troops had no delay or obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Lide filled in the road and built bridges, and the army advanced without delay.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚悅。

translations.literal: Taizong was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋受詔造翠微宮及玉華宮，咸稱旨，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Before long he received an edict to build Cuwei Palace and Yuhua Palace; all accorded with the imperial will, and rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to build Cuwei Palace and Yuhua Palace. Both projects met with the emperor's approval, and he received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 俄遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，攝司空，營護太宗山陵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he acted as Minister of Works and oversaw Taizong's imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In 649 he served as acting Minister of Works and supervised construction of Taizong's tomb.

sentences.zh: 事畢，進封為公。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was complete his title was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年卒，贈吏部尚書、并州都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he died; posthumously granted Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Area Commander of Bing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 656 and was posthumously honored as Minister of State and area commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄邃子，官至司農少卿。

translations.literal: His son Xuansui reached the office of Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuansui rose to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 玄邃子知微，聖歷初，歷位右豹韜衛將軍。

translations.literal: Xuansui's son Zhiwei, at the beginning of Shengli, successively held the post of General of the Right Leopard-Bow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xuansui's son Zhiwei served under Empress Wu as general of the Right Leopard-Bow Guard.

sentences.zh: 時突厥默啜有女請和親，則天令淮陽王武延秀往納其女，命知微攝春官尚書送赴虜廷。

translations.literal: At that time the Türk Mo-ch'o had a daughter who requested marriage alliance; Zetian ordered Prince Huaiyang Wu Yanxiu to go receive her daughter, and ordered Zhiwei to act as Minister of Spring Office and escort them to the barbarians' court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türk chieftain Mo-ch'o sought a marriage alliance, Empress Wu sent Prince Huaiyang Wu Yanxiu to receive his daughter and appointed Zhiwei acting Minister of Rites to escort the party to the Türk court.

sentences.zh: 默啜以延秀非皇室諸王，大怒，遂拘之別所，與知微率眾自恆岳道攻陷趙、定二州。

translations.literal: Mo-ch'o because Yanxiu was not a prince of the imperial house was greatly enraged; then he detained him in a separate place, and with Zhiwei led troops by the Heng Mountains route to attack and capture Zhao and Ding prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Mo-ch'o was furious that Yanxiu was not a prince of the imperial clan. He imprisoned him separately, then joined Zhiwei in leading troops down the Heng Mountains route to capture Zhao and Ding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 知微經歲余自突厥所還，則天以其隨賊入寇，令百官臠割，然後斬之，並夷其三族。

translations.literal: After more than a year Zhiwei returned from the Türk place; Zetian because he had followed the bandits in invasion ordered the hundred officials to carve and dismember him, then behead him, and also exterminate his three clans.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Zhiwei returned from Türk captivity. Empress Wu, holding that he had aided the enemy invasion, ordered the officials to carve his flesh before beheading him and exterminated his clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 立本，顯慶中累遷將作大匠，後代立德為工部尚書，兄弟相代為八座，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Liben, in the Xianqing era was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Palace Construction; later he replaced Lide as Minister of Works; the brothers in succession held one of the eight seats, and opinion of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: Liben rose to Grand Master of Palace Construction during Xianqing and later succeeded his brother Lide as Minister of Works. The brothers held one of the eight highest offices in turn—a distinction widely admired.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，遷右相，賜爵博陵縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang he was moved to Right Chancellor and granted the title Baron of Boling county.
translations.idiomatic: In 668 he was appointed Right Chancellor and enfeoffed Baron of Boling.

sentences.zh: 立本雖有應務之才，而尤善圖畫，工於寫真。

translations.literal: Liben though had talent for responding to affairs, yet was especially skilled in painting and drawing, adept at portraiture.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liben was capable in administrative affairs, he was above all a painter, especially skilled at portraiture.

sentences.zh: 《秦府十八學士圖》及貞觀中《凌煙閣功臣圖》，並立本之跡也，時人咸稱其妙。

translations.literal: The "Eighteen Scholars of the Qin Prince's Mansion" and the "Meritorious Ministers of Lingyan Pavilion" of the Zhenguan era were all Liben's traces; people of the time all praised their wonder.
translations.idiomatic: The "Eighteen Scholars of the Qin Prince's Mansion" and the Zhenguan-era "Meritorious Ministers of Lingyan Pavilion" were both his work, and contemporaries acclaimed their excellence.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗與侍臣學士泛舟於春苑，池中有異鳥，隨波容與。

translations.literal: Taizong once with attending ministers and academicians floated in boats on the Spring Garden; in the pond there was an unusual bird, drifting with the waves at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once went boating on the Spring Garden pond with his ministers and scholars. An unusual bird floated at ease upon the waves.

sentences.zh: 太宗擊賞，數詔座者為詠，召立本令寫焉。

translations.literal: Taizong struck in appreciation; several times he edicted those seated to compose verse, and summoned Liben ordering him to depict it.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Taizong had those present compose poems about it and summoned Liben to paint the scene.

sentences.zh: 時閣外傳呼云：「畫師閻立本。」

translations.literal: At that time outside the pavilion a voice called: "The painter Yan Liben."
translations.idiomatic: From outside the hall came the call, "The painter Yan Liben—"

sentences.zh: 時已為主爵郎中，奔走流汗，俯伏池側，手揮丹粉，瞻望座賓，不勝愧赧。

translations.literal: He was already Master of Principal Honored Ranks; he ran sweating, prostrated himself beside the pond, waved cinnabar powder with his hand, gazed up at the seated guests, and could not bear the shame.
translations.idiomatic: By then he already held the rank of Master of Principal Honored Ranks. He ran up sweating, knelt by the pond, and painted with cinnabar while stealing glances at the guests—overcome with humiliation.

sentences.zh: 退誡其子曰：「吾少好讀書，倖免面牆，緣情染翰，頗及儕流。

translations.literal: Retiring he admonished his sons, saying: "I from youth loved reading books and by luck escaped facing the wall; following feeling I touched the brush and somewhat reached the level of my peers.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he warned his sons, "I loved books from youth and was fortunate enough to receive a proper education. I took up the brush as well and kept pace with my peers.

sentences.zh: 唯以丹青見知，躬廝役之務，辱莫大焉！

translations.literal: Only because of painting and drawing was I known; personally performing menial tasks—no disgrace is greater!
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am known only for painting and am summoned to perform the work of a servant. There is no greater disgrace!

sentences.zh: 汝宜深誡，勿習此末伎。」

translations.literal: You ought deeply to take warning—do not study this inferior art."
translations.idiomatic: Take this to heart and do not learn this low craft."

sentences.zh: 立本為性所好，欲罷不能也。

translations.literal: Painting was what Liben's nature loved; he wished to stop but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Yet painting was Liben's true passion, and he could not bring himself to give it up.

sentences.zh: 及為右相，與左相姜恪對掌樞密。

translations.literal: When he became Right Chancellor he paired with Left Chancellor Jiang Kuo in jointly holding the keys of state.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Chancellor he shared control of state affairs with Left Chancellor Jiang Kuo.

sentences.zh: 恪既歷任將軍，立功塞外；

translations.literal: Kuo had successively served as general and established merit beyond the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Kuo had served as a general and won distinction on the frontier;

sentences.zh: 立本唯善於圖畫，非宰輔之器。

translations.literal: Liben was skilled only in painting and drawing—not the material of chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liben was known only for painting—not the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 故時人以《千字文》為語曰：「左相宣威沙漠，右相馳譽丹青。」

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time used the Thousand-Character Classic as a saying: "The left chancellor spreads might in the desert; the right chancellor gallops in fame through painting."
translations.idiomatic: People of the day summed it up in a line from the Thousand-Character Classic: "The left chancellor spreads his fame across the desert; the right chancellor wins renown with his brush."

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，百司復舊名，改為中書令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng the hundred offices restored their old names; he was changed to Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 670, when offices reverted to their former titles, he was redesignated Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 673.

sentences.zh: 柳亨，蒲州解人，魏尚書左僕射慶之孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Heng, a man of Jie in Pu prefecture, was the grandson of Qingzhi, Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heng was a native of Jie County in Puzhou and the grandson of Liu Qingzhi, Wei Left Vice Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 父旦，隋太常少卿、新城縣公。

translations.literal: His father Dan was Sui Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Duke of Xincheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan had served as Sui Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Duke of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 亨，隋末歷熊耳、王屋二縣長，陷於李密。

translations.literal: Heng, at the end of Sui successively served as magistrate of Xiong'er and Wangwu counties and fell into Li Mi's hands.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, Heng served as magistrate of Xiong'er and Wangwu counties and was caught up in Li Mi's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 密敗歸國，累授駕部郎中。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated he returned to the state and was repeatedly appointed Master of the Transport Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi's defeat he submitted to the Tang and was appointed master of the transport bureau.

sentences.zh: 亨容貌魁偉，高祖甚愛重之，特以殿中監竇誕之女妻焉，即帝之外孫也。

translations.literal: Heng's appearance was towering and grand; Gaozu greatly loved and valued him, and specially gave him in marriage the daughter of Palace Attendant Dou Yan—she was the emperor's maternal granddaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was tall and imposing. Gaozu favored him greatly and gave him the daughter of Palace Attendant Dou Yan in marriage—she was the emperor's maternal granddaughter.

sentences.zh: 三遷左衛中郎將，封壽陵縣男。

translations.literal: Three promotions later he was Colonel of the Left Guard and enfeoffed Baron of Shouling county.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became colonel of the Left Guard and was enfeoffed Baron of Shouling.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以譴出為邛州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, because of censure he was sent out as Prefect of Qiong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was demoted to prefect of Qiongzhou after being censured.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，被代還，數年不調。

translations.literal: He was added Regular Attendant; when replaced and returned, for several years he received no new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added title of regular attendant, but after his term ended he went several years without a new posting.

sentences.zh: 因兄葬，遇太宗游於南山，召見與語，頗哀矜之。

translations.literal: Because of his elder brother's burial he encountered Taizong touring at South Mountain; summoned to audience and conversed with, Taizong greatly pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: While attending his elder brother's funeral he met Taizong on an outing to South Mountain. The emperor summoned him, spoke with him, and was deeply moved by his circumstances.

sentences.zh: 數日，北門引見，深加誨獎，拜銀青光祿大夫，行光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Several days later he was led in audience at the North Gate; deeply admonished and rewarded, he was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments, acting Vice Minister of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Taizong received him at the North Gate, exhorted and rewarded him, and appointed him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments, acting as vice minister of the same office.

sentences.zh: 太宗每誡之曰：「與卿舊親，情素兼宿，卿為人交遊過多，今授此職，宜存簡靜。」

translations.literal: Taizong each time admonished him: "With you I have old kinship; feeling has always been deep; you as a man have too many social connections—now granting this office, you ought to preserve simplicity and quiet."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong repeatedly warned him, "We are old kin, and I have long held you dear. You keep too wide a circle of friends. In this new office you must live simply and quietly."

sentences.zh: 亨性好射獵，有饕湎之名。

translations.literal: Heng by nature loved archery and hunting and had a name for gluttony and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Heng loved archery and hunting and had a reputation for gluttony and heavy drinking.

sentences.zh: 此後頗自勖勵，杜絕賓客，約身節儉，勤於職事。

translations.literal: After this he greatly encouraged himself, cut off guests entirely, restrained himself in thrift, and was diligent in official affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he applied himself rigorously, stopped entertaining guests, lived frugally, and devoted himself to his duties.

sentences.zh: 太宗亦以此稱之。

translations.literal: Taizong also for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised him for the change.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以修太廟功，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, for merit in repairing the Grand Ancestral Temple, he was added Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments with the Gold-Gleaming rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 649, for his work on the imperial ancestral temple, he was promoted to gold-gleaming grand master of imperial entertainments.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜太常卿，從幸萬年宮，檢校岐州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices; he followed on an imperial visit to Wannian Palace and acted as Prefect of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, accompanied the emperor to Wannian Palace, and served as acting prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年卒，贈禮部尚書、幽州都督，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui he died; posthumously granted Minister of Rites and Area Commander of You prefecture; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 655 and was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites and area commander of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 亨族子范，貞觀中為侍御史。

translations.literal: Heng's clansman Fan, in the Zhenguan era served as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's clansman Fan served as an attending censor during the Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 時吳王恪好畋獵，損居人，范奏彈之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Wu of Wu loved hunting; he harmed residents; Fan memorialized and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wu of Wu indulged in hunting and harmed local residents, Fan memorialized the throne to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 太宗因謂侍臣：「權萬紀事我兒，不能匡正，其罪合死。」

translations.literal: Taizong therefore said to attending ministers: "Quan Wanji served my son yet could not correct him—his crime merits death."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then told his ministers, "Quan Wanji attends my son yet failed to correct him. That is a capital offense."

sentences.zh: 范進曰：「房玄齡事陛下，猶不能諫止畋獵，豈可獨罪萬紀？」

translations.literal: Fan advanced and said: "Fang Xuanling served Your Majesty yet also could not remonstrate and stop the hunting—how can Wanji alone be blamed?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied, "Fang Xuanling serves Your Majesty yet could not stop your own hunting. How can Wanji alone be punished?"

sentences.zh: 太宗大怒，拂衣而入。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly enraged, brushed his robes and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong flew into a rage, shook off his robes, and stalked off.

sentences.zh: 久之，獨引范謂曰：「何得逆折我？」

translations.literal: After a long while he alone summoned Fan and said: "How dare you confront and refute me?"
translations.idiomatic: After some time he summoned Fan alone and said, "How dare you talk back to me so bluntly?"

sentences.zh: 范曰：「臣聞主聖臣直，陛下仁明，臣敢不盡愚直。」

translations.literal: Fan said: "Your servant hears that when the lord is sage the minister is straight; Your Majesty is benevolent and clear—how could your servant not exhaust foolish straightness?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan answered, "I have heard that when the ruler is wise the minister speaks plainly. Your Majesty is benevolent and enlightened—how could I fail to speak my mind?"

sentences.zh: 太宗意乃解。

translations.literal: Taizong's mind then was released.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 范，高宗時歷位尚書右丞、揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Fan, in Gaozong's era successively held the posts of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Yang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, Fan served as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and chief administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 亨兄子奭。

translations.literal: Heng's elder brother's son Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, nephew of Heng's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 奭父則，隋左衛騎曹，因使卒於高麗。

translations.literal: Shi's father Ze was Left Guard Cavalry Adjutant in Sui; because of a mission he died in Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's father Ze had served as Sui cavalry adjutant of the Left Guard and died in Goguryeo while on an embassy.

sentences.zh: 奭入蕃迎喪柩，哀號逾禮，深為夷人所慕。

translations.literal: Shi entered the barbarian lands to receive the funeral bier; his wailing exceeded the rites, and he was deeply admired by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Shi went into Goguryeo to bring back his father's coffin, mourning with such unrestrained grief that it exceeded proper ritual—and the foreigners deeply admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he rose through successive appointments to the post of Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 後以外生女為皇太子妃，擢拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Later, because his niece by his sister's marriage became the crown prince's consort, he was abruptly promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After his sister's daughter became consort to the crown prince, he was elevated to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 妃為皇后，奭又遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the consort became empress, Shi was again transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When she was made empress, Shi was promoted again, this time to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，代褚遂良為中書令，仍監修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he replaced Chu Suiliang as Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, and concurrently supervised the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 3 (652) he succeeded Chu Suiliang as director of the Secretariat and was also put in charge of compiling the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 俄而後漸見疏忌，奭憂懼，頻上疏請辭樞密之任，轉為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long the empress was gradually seen to be estranged and suspected; Shi grew anxious and fearful, repeatedly submitting memorials requesting release from the pivotal-secret duties, and was transferred to Minister of the Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Empress Wang fell from favor; alarmed, Shi repeatedly memorialized the throne asking to be relieved of his confidential duties at court and was reassigned as minister of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 及後廢，累貶愛州刺史。

translations.literal: When the empress was deposed, he was repeatedly demoted to prefect of Ai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress was deposed, he was stripped of rank repeatedly until he was sent as prefect of Ai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋為許敬宗、李義府所構，雲奭潛通宮掖，謀行鴆毒，又與褚遂良等朋黨構扇，罪當大逆。

translations.literal: Soon he was framed by Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, who claimed that Shi had secretly communicated with the inner palace, plotted to administer poison, and moreover formed a faction with Chu Suiliang and others to incite trouble—the crime meriting great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu manufactured charges that Shi had been in secret contact with the inner palace and was plotting poison, and that he had conspired in a clique with Chu Suiliang and others—a capital offense of treason.

sentences.zh: 高宗遣使就愛州殺之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Gaozong dispatched envoys to Ai Prefecture to kill him and confiscated his household property.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong sent agents to Ai Prefecture to execute him and seized all his family's assets.

sentences.zh: 奭既死非其罪，甚為當時之所傷痛。

translations.literal: Since Shi died for a crime he had not committed, people of the time were deeply pained.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had died for crimes he did not commit, and the injustice deeply grieved men of the time.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，則天遺制，與褚遂良、韓瑗等並還官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, by Wu Zetian's testamentary edict, his offices and titles were restored along with those of Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenlong era, Wu Zetian's posthumous edict restored official rank to him together with Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 子孫親屬當時緣坐者，咸從曠蕩。

translations.literal: Descendants and relatives who at the time had been implicated by association were all included in a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: All descendants and kin who had been punished by association were fully pardoned under the general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 開元初，亨孫渙為中書舍人，表曰：「臣堂伯祖奭，去明慶三年，與褚遂良等五家同被譴戮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Heng's grandson Huan served as Secretariat Drafter and submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant's hall great-uncle Shi, in the third year past of Mingqing, together with five families including Chu Suiliang, was jointly subjected to punitive execution.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era Liu Huan, grandson of Liu Heng, wrote as a Secretariat drafter: "Your servant's grand-uncle Shi, in the third year of Xianqing, was executed along with four other families including Chu Suiliang's.

sentences.zh: 雖蒙遺制蕩雪，而子孫亡沒並盡。

translations.literal: Although they received cleansing under the testamentary edict, descendants died out altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Though the posthumous amnesty cleared their names, every descendant had perished.

sentences.zh: 唯有曾孫無忝，見貫龔州，蒙雪多年，猶同遠竄。

translations.literal: Only the great-great-grandson Wutan, registered in Gong Prefecture, though cleared of guilt for many years, was still treated like one banished far away.
translations.idiomatic: Only the great-great-grandson Wutan survived, registered in exile at Gong Prefecture; though exonerated years ago, he still lived as though banished to the farthest margins.

sentences.zh: 陛下自臨宇縣，優政必被，鴻恩及於泉壤，大造加於亡絕。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty personally assumed rule over the realm, benevolent governance must extend everywhere; vast grace reaches even the springs and soil, and great creation is granted to those extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, your gracious rule has reached every corner of the empire, your boundless kindness even to the dead beneath the earth, and new life to families that had been wiped out.

sentences.zh: 先天已後，頻降絲綸，曾任宰相之家，並許收其淪滯。

translations.literal: After Xiantian, imperial edicts were frequently issued, and families that had once produced chancellors were all permitted to recover their fallen and stranded members.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiantian era you have issued edict after edict allowing families of former chancellors to recall kin who had languished in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 況臣伯祖往叨執政，無犯受誅，藁窆尚隔故鄉，後嗣遂編蠻服。

translations.literal: Moreover, your servant's grand-uncle once held the reins of government, yet was executed though he had committed no crime; his straw-wrapped coffin still lies apart from his native place, and his descendants have been registered among the southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: My grand-uncle once served at the highest level of government yet was put to death though guilty of nothing; his coffin still lies far from his homeland, and his heirs have been enrolled among the distant southern register.

sentences.zh: 臣不申號訴，義所難安。

translations.literal: If your servant does not lodge this cry of appeal, righteousness makes it hard to be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not make this appeal, I cannot live with myself.

sentences.zh: 伏乞許臣伯祖還葬鄉里，其曾孫無忝放歸本貫。」

translations.literal: Your servant humbly begs permission for your servant's grand-uncle to be returned and buried in his home district, and for the great-great-grandson Wutan to be released and restored to his original register.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that my grand-uncle be permitted burial in his native district, and that Wutan be allowed to return to his proper registry.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，敕令奭歸葬，官造靈輿遞還。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; an edict ordered Shi's return for burial, with the government constructing a spirit carriage to transport him back by relay stages.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was accepted. An imperial order directed that Shi be brought home for burial, with an official funeral carriage sent by relay to convey his remains.

sentences.zh: 無忝後歷位潭州都督。

translations.literal: Wutan later successively held the post of military commissioner of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wutan later served as military commissioner of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 渙弟澤，景雲中為右率府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: Huan's younger brother Ze, in the Jingyun era served as Army Equipment Section Officer of the Right Guard Office.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's younger brother Liu Ze served during the Jingyun era as equipment officer in the Right Guard directorate.

sentences.zh: 先是，姚元之、宋璟知政事，奏請停中宗朝斜封官數千員。

translations.literal: Previously, Yao Yuanzhi and Song Jing managed state affairs and memorialized requesting cessation of several thousand "slanted-seal" officials from Zhongzong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yao Yuanzhi and Song Jing held power, they had petitioned to dismiss the several thousand irregular appointees of Emperor Zhongzong's "slanted seal" era.

sentences.zh: 及元之等出為刺史，太平公主又特為之言，有敕總令復舊職。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhi and the others went out as prefects, Princess Taiping again spoke specially on their behalf, and an edict ordered all to resume their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao and Song were sent out as regional prefects, Princess Taiping interceded for the dismissed officials, and an edict restored them all to their former posts.

sentences.zh: 澤上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Ze submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ze memorialized the throne in protest:

sentences.zh: 臣聞藥不毒，不可以蠲疾；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that medicine without toxicity cannot eliminate illness;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that medicine must be bitter to cure disease;

sentences.zh: 詞不切，不可以補過。

translations.literal: words without sharpness cannot remedy faults.
translations.idiomatic: and words must be blunt to set things right.

sentences.zh: 是以習甘旨者，非攝養之方；

translations.literal: Therefore one who is accustomed to sweet delicacies has no method of nourishing the body;
translations.idiomatic: Those who feed only on sweetness know nothing of true nourishment;

sentences.zh: 邇諛佞者，積危殆之本。

translations.literal: one who draws near to flattery and sycophancy accumulates the root of peril and danger.
translations.idiomatic: those who keep flatterers close are hoarding the seeds of ruin.

sentences.zh: 臣實愚朴，志懷剛勵，或聞政之不當，事之不直，常慷慨關心，夢寐懷憤。

translations.literal: Your servant is truly simple and plain, but in will harbors resolute strength; whenever I hear of governance that is improper or affairs that are unjust, I am often moved with passionate concern and carry indignation even in sleep and dreams.
translations.idiomatic: I am no clever courtier, but my conscience is stiff: whenever I hear of wrong policy or crooked conduct, it burns in me waking and sleeping alike.

sentences.zh: 每願殉身以諫，伏死而爭。

translations.literal: I always wish to give my body in remonstrance, to lie prostrate and die in contention.
translations.idiomatic: I would gladly risk my life to speak out, die face down if I must, but speak I will.

sentences.zh: 但利於社稷，有便於君上，雖蒙禍被難，殺身不悔也。

translations.literal: So long as it benefits the altars of state and is useful to the sovereign, even if I suffer calamity and hardship, I would not regret giving my life.
translations.idiomatic: If it serves the realm and the throne, no penalty would make me regret it.

sentences.zh: 竊見神龍以來，群邪作孽，法網不振，綱維大紊，實由內寵專命，外嬖擅權，因貴憑寵，賣官鬻爵。

translations.literal: I have privately observed that since Shenlong, wicked men have wrought calamity, the net of law has not been taut, and the cords of governance have been greatly tangled—truly because inner favorites held sole command and outer minions usurped power, relying on rank and depending on favor to sell offices and barter titles.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Shenlong era I have watched corruption run wild—the law in shreds, order in ruins—because palace favorites monopolized power and royal intimates sold rank and office to the highest bidder.

sentences.zh: 硃紫之榮，出於僕妾之口；

translations.literal: The glory of vermilion and purple robes issued from the mouths of maids and concubines;
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet and purple robes were dispensed on a servant girl's whim;

sentences.zh: 賞罰之命，乖於章程之典。

translations.literal: orders of reward and punishment departed from the standards of regulation and code.
translations.idiomatic: rewards and punishments bore no relation to the statutes.

sentences.zh: 妃主之門，有同商賈；

translations.literal: The gates of imperial consorts were like those of merchants;
translations.idiomatic: The consorts' households traded like market stalls;

sentences.zh: 舉選之署，實均阛阓。

translations.literal: the offices of selection for office were truly no different from market streets.
translations.idiomatic: the Board of Civil Appointments might as well have been a bazaar.

sentences.zh: 屠販之子，悉由邪而忝官；

translations.literal: Sons of butchers and peddlers all unworthily received office through wicked paths;
translations.idiomatic: Butchers' sons bought their way into office;

sentences.zh: 黜斥之人，咸因奸而冒進。

translations.literal: Persons who had been dismissed all advanced improperly through wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: dismissed criminals clawed their way back through bribery and intrigue.

sentences.zh: 天下為亂，社稷幾危，賴陛下聰明神武，拯其將墜。

translations.literal: The realm was thrown into turmoil, and the altars of state were nearly endangered; it relied on Your Majesty's intelligence, spirit, and martial prowess to save what was about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: The empire teetered on the brink; only Your Majesty's wisdom and force pulled it back from the edge.

sentences.zh: 此陛下耳目之所親擊，固可永為炯誡者也。

translations.literal: This is something Your Majesty's eyes and ears have personally witnessed—it can indeed be an eternal bright warning.
translations.idiomatic: You saw this with your own eyes; let it stand forever as a warning.

sentences.zh: 臣聞作法於理，猶恐其亂，作法於亂，誰能救之？

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: to make laws in times of order, one still fears disorder; to make laws in times of disorder—who can rescue them?
translations.idiomatic: They say: even in good times, bad precedent is dangerous; establish bad precedent in troubled times and who can undo it?

sentences.zh: 只如斜封授官，皆是僕妾汲引，迷謬先帝，昧目前朝，豈是孝和情之所憐，心之所愛？

translations.literal: Take for instance the slanted-seal appointments—all were drawn up by maids and concubines, misleading and deluding the late emperor and blinding the present court. Could these truly have been what Xiaohe's feelings pitied and his heart loved?
translations.idiomatic: The "slanted seal" appointments were procured by servants and concubines—they deluded the late emperor and stain the present reign. Did Emperor Zhongzong truly cherish these men?

sentences.zh: 陛下初即位時，納姚元之、宋璟之計，所以咸令黜之。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first took the throne, you adopted the plans of Yao Yuanzhi and Song Jing, and therefore ordered them all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When you first ascended the throne you followed Yao Yuanzhi and Song Jing's counsel and dismissed them all.

sentences.zh: 頃日已來，又令敘之。

translations.literal: In recent days you have again ordered them ranked and restored.
translations.idiomatic: Recently you have ordered them restored.

sentences.zh: 將謂為斜封之人不忍棄也，以為先帝之意不可違也？

translations.literal: Are you saying that you cannot bear to abandon the slanted-seal men, and that the late emperor's intent cannot be violated?
translations.idiomatic: Is it because you cannot bear to cast them aside—or because you feel bound by the late emperor's wishes?

sentences.zh: 若斜封之人不忍棄也，是韋月將、燕欽融之流亦不可褒贈也，李多祚、鄭克義之徒亦不可清雪也。

translations.literal: If the slanted-seal men cannot be abandoned, then men like Wei Yuejiang and Yan Qinrong likewise cannot be posthumously honored; men like Li Duozuo and Zheng Keyi likewise cannot be cleared and rehabilitated.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot abandon these appointees, then you cannot honor Wei Yuejiang and Yan Qinrong, nor clear the names of Li Duozuo and Zheng Keyi.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不能忍於此而獨能忍於彼？

translations.literal: Why can Your Majesty not bear it in these cases yet alone can bear it in those?
translations.idiomatic: Why is your forbearance reserved only for the corrupt?

sentences.zh: 使善惡不定，反覆相攻，使君子道消，小人道長，為邪者獲利，為正者銜冤，奈何導人以為非，勸人以為僻？

translations.literal: This makes good and evil unsettled, reversal and attack each other, makes the way of the noble man wane and the way of the petty man grow, lets the wicked profit and the upright harbor grievance—why guide people toward wrong and encourage them toward depravity?
translations.idiomatic: You leave good and evil in flux, the upright silenced and the crooked rewarded—why teach the realm that vice pays and virtue does not?

sentences.zh: 將何以懲風俗，將何以止奸邪？

translations.literal: With what will you chastise custom, with what will you stop wickedness and evil?
translations.idiomatic: How then will you reform public morals or restrain corruption?

sentences.zh: 今海內咸稱太平公主令胡僧慧范曲引此輩，將有誤於陛下矣。

translations.literal: Now throughout the realm all say that Princess Taiping ordered the barbarian monk Huifan to coax and lead this crowd—they are about to mislead Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The empire whispers that Princess Taiping used the monk Huifan to manipulate these appointments—and to mislead you.

sentences.zh: 謗議盈耳，咨嗟滿衢，故語曰：「姚、宋為相，邪不如正。

translations.literal: Slander and discussion fill the ears, sighs and laments fill the streets; hence the saying: "Under Yao and Song as chancellors, the wicked did not prevail over the upright.
translations.idiomatic: The streets buzz with complaint, and people say: "When Yao and Song governed, vice gave way to virtue.

sentences.zh: 太平用事，正不如邪。」

translations.literal: Under Taiping's influence, the upright did not prevail over the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Under Princess Taiping, virtue gives way to vice.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「無偏無陂，遵王之義，無反無側，王道正直。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Without partiality, without slope—follow the king's righteousness; without perversity, without deviation—the king's way is straight."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Without partiality or bias, follow the royal way; without crookedness or deviation, the king's path is straight."

sentences.zh: 臣恐因循，流近致遠，積小為大，累微起高。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that through inertia, what flows near reaches far, what accumulates small becomes great, what piles slight rises high.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that small concessions now will swell into great calamity—that neglect today breeds disaster tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 勿謂何傷，其禍將長；

translations.literal: Do not say "what harm"—the calamity will grow;
translations.idiomatic: Do not ask "what harm can it do"—the harm will grow;

sentences.zh: 勿謂何害，其禍將大。

translations.literal: do not say "what injury"—the calamity will be great.
translations.idiomatic: do not ask "what damage"—the damage will be vast.

sentences.zh: 又賞罰之典，紀綱不謬，天秩有禮，君爵有功，不可因怒以妄罰，不可因喜以妄賞。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the canon of rewards and punishments, the threads of governance must not err; heaven's order has ritual, the ruler's enfeoffment has merit—it is impermissible to punish rashly from anger, impermissible to reward rashly from joy.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments are the backbone of government: rank must follow merit, never rage or favor. You must not punish in anger nor reward on whim.

sentences.zh: 伏見尚醫奉御彭君慶，以邪巫小道，超授三品，奈何輕用名器，加非其才？

translations.literal: Your servant has observed the Chief Imperial Physician Peng Junqing, through wicked sorcery and petty arts, abruptly granted the third rank—how can you lightly use exalted instruments of office on one whose talent does not warrant it?
translations.idiomatic: I see that Peng Junqing, the chief imperial physician, was leapfrogged to the third rank for sorcery and mumbo-jumbo—how can such a precious office be wasted on unworthy hands?

sentences.zh: 昔公主為子求郎，明帝不許；

translations.literal: In the past when a princess sought a gentleman for her son, Emperor Ming did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: When a princess once asked Emperor Ming to make her son a court gentleman, he refused;

sentences.zh: 今聖朝私愛，賞及憸人。

translations.literal: now in our sagely court private affection extends rewards even to vicious men.
translations.idiomatic: today private favor extends even to the venal.

sentences.zh: 董狐不亡，豈有所隱？

translations.literal: If Dong Hu had not perished, would anything be hidden?
translations.idiomatic: If Dong Hu still walked among us, could this be concealed from the annals?

sentences.zh: 臣聞賞一人而千萬人悅者賞之，罰一人而千萬人勸者罰之。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: reward one man and if ten thousand men rejoice, reward him; punish one man and if ten thousand men are encouraged, punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The wise ruler rewards where the multitude approves and punishes where the multitude is satisfied.

sentences.zh: 臣雖未睹聖朝之妄罰，已睹聖朝之妄賞矣，《書》曰：「官不及私暱，惟其能；

translations.literal: Your servant, though I have not yet seen rash punishment in our sagely court, have already seen rash rewards. The Book of Documents says: "Offices do not reach private favorites—only the capable;
translations.idiomatic: I have not yet seen wrongful punishments under this reign, but I have seen wrongful rewards. The Book of Documents says: "Office goes not to personal favorites, but to the capable;

sentences.zh: 爵罔及惡德，惟其賢。」

translations.literal: enfeoffment does not reach men of evil virtue—only the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: rank never touches the wicked, but only the worthy.

sentences.zh: 臣恐近習之人為其先容，有謬於陛下也。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that persons near at hand acted as go-betweens for them and have misled Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear those closest to you may have paved the way and led you astray.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下熟思而察之。

translations.literal: I only ask Your Majesty to ponder deeply and examine it.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 雖往者不可諫，而來者猶可追。

translations.literal: Though what is past cannot be remonstrated about, what is to come can still be pursued and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: What is done is done—but what lies ahead can still be set right.

sentences.zh: 願杜請謁之路，塞恩幸之門，鑑誡前非，無累後悔。

translations.literal: I wish to block the path of petitioning for favor, to stop up the gate of grace and favor, to take warning from past wrongs and not accumulate later regret.
translations.idiomatic: Close the doors to favor-seeking, shut off the paths of private patronage, learn from past mistakes, and spare yourself future regret.

sentences.zh: 申畫一之法，明不二之刑，不詢之謀勿庸，無稽之言勿應，則天下之化，人無間焉，日新之德，天鑑不遠。

translations.literal: Declare unified law, make clear undivided punishments; do not employ plans not deliberated, do not respond to words without basis—then the transformation of the realm will leave no gap among the people, the virtue of daily renewal, heaven's mirror is not far.
translations.idiomatic: Uphold uniform law, apply justice without exception, heed no counsel undeliberated and no rumor unfounded—then the realm will be transformed without division, your virtue renewed day by day, under heaven's approving gaze.

sentences.zh: 澤後參選，會有敕令選人上書陳事，將加收擢，澤又上書曰：

translations.literal: Ze later participated in selection; it happened that an edict ordered selection candidates to submit memorials stating affairs, intending additional promotion and elevation—Ze again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Later, while Liu Ze was undergoing examination for office, an edict invited candidates to submit memorials on public affairs with promotion promised in return. Liu Ze wrote again:

sentences.zh: 頃者韋氏險诐，奸臣同惡。

translations.literal: Recently the Wei clan was dangerous and perverse, wicked ministers shared their evil.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago the Wei faction was treacherous and wicked ministers joined in their crimes.

sentences.zh: 賞罰紊弛，綱紀紛綸，政以賄成，官因寵進，言正者獲戾，行殊者見疑，海內寒心，實將莫救。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments were tangled and slack, the cords of governance were confused and tangled, government was accomplished through bribes, offices advanced through favor, those who spoke rightly incurred blame, those whose conduct was exceptional were suspected—the realm chilled at heart and truly would soon have been beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments collapsed, discipline unraveled, office bought with bribes and rank granted through favor; honest speech brought punishment and integrity bred suspicion—the realm lost heart and stood on the verge of ruin.

sentences.zh: 賴神明佑德，宗廟降靈，天討有罪，人用不保，陛下睿謀神聖，勇智聰明，安宗廟於已危，拯黎庶於將溺。

translations.literal: It relied on the divine spirit's protection of virtue, the ancestral temple's descent of numinous power, heaven's punishment of the guilty, and men's failure to preserve themselves—Your Majesty's wise plans were divine and sagely, brave and intelligent, settling the ancestral temple when already endangered, saving the common people when about to drown.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven protected the righteous, the ancestral spirits intervened, and Your Majesty—with sacred wisdom, courage, and clarity—saved the altars of state from collapse and the people from drowning.

sentences.zh: 今尨眉鮐背，歡欣踴躍，望聖朝之撫輯，聽聖朝之德音。

translations.literal: Now the white-browed and humpbacked leap for joy in exultation, looking to the sagely court's calming governance and listening to the sagely court's virtuous pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: Now gray-haired elders leap for joy, awaiting the court's benevolent rule and hanging on every word of its virtuous decrees.

sentences.zh: 今陛下蠲煩省徭，法明德舉，萬邦愷樂，室家胥慶。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has cleared away burdens and reduced corvée, clarified the law and elevated the virtuous; the myriad states are harmonious and joyful, every household alike celebrates.
translations.idiomatic: You have eased burdens, lightened labor, clarified the law, and elevated the worthy—the empire rejoices and every household celebrates.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞危者保其存也，亂者有其理也。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard: the endangered preserve their existence; the chaotic have their principles of order.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that those in peril must guard what keeps them alive, and those in disorder must hold fast to principle.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下安不忘危，理不忘亂，存不忘亡，則克享天心，國家長保矣。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers that if Your Majesty is secure yet does not forget danger, in order yet does not forget chaos, in existence yet does not forget extinction—then you can enjoy heaven's heart and the state will be long preserved.
translations.idiomatic: If in security you remember danger, in order you remember chaos, in survival you remember extinction, you will enjoy heaven's favor and the state will endure.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「罔不有初，鮮克有終。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "There is nothing without a beginning—rarely is there completion to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "Everything has a beginning; few see it through to the end.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下慎厥終，修其初，非禮勿視，非禮勿動。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers that Your Majesty should be careful of the end, cultivate the beginning, not look upon what is not ritual, not act upon what is not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Guard the ending as carefully as the beginning: do not look on what is unseemly, do not act on what is unseemly.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「惟德罔小，萬邦惟慶，惟不德罔大，墜厥宗。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Only virtue, though small—the myriad states have rejoicing; only lack of virtue, though great—fall his ancestral lineage.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "No virtue is too slight to bring the realm joy; no wickedness is too great to overturn a dynasty.

sentences.zh: 甚可畏也，甚可懼也，伏惟陛下慎之哉！

translations.literal: Greatly to be feared! Greatly to be dreaded! Your servant respectfully asks Your Majesty to be careful!
translations.idiomatic: This is deeply terrifying—I beg Your Majesty to heed it!

sentences.zh: 夫驕奢起於親貴，綱紀亂於寵幸。

translations.literal: Now arrogance and extravagance rise from kin and the honored; the cords of governance are disturbed by favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Pride and extravagance arise among the royal kin; discipline collapses where favorites hold sway.

sentences.zh: 願陛下禁之於親貴，則天下隨風矣；

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to forbid it among kin and the honored—then all under heaven will follow the wind;
translations.idiomatic: Restrain them among the kin and nobility, and the realm will follow your lead;

sentences.zh: 制之於寵幸，則天下法明矣。

translations.literal: to restrain it among favorites—then all under heaven's law will be clear.
translations.idiomatic: restrain them among the favorites, and the law will be clear to all.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「刑於寡妻，至於兄弟，以御於家邦。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "A model to the solitary wife, extending to the brothers, to govern the family and state.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "He sets an example for his wife, then for his brothers, and so governs family and state.

sentences.zh: 若親貴為之而不禁，寵幸撓之而見從，是政之不常，令之不一，則奸詐斯起，暴亂生焉。

translations.literal: If kin and the honored do it yet it is not forbidden, if favorites interfere and are obeyed—then governance is not constant and orders are not uniform; then treachery and deceit arise and violence and disorder are born.
translations.idiomatic: If the nobility may do as they please and favorites may override the law, policy becomes capricious and orders contradictory—fraud flourishes and violence follows.

sentences.zh: 雖嚴刑峻制，朝施暮戮，而法不行矣。

translations.literal: Even with severe punishments and stern regulations, executions in the morning and at evening—the law would still not be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Even the harshest penalties, carried out morning and night, would not make the law prevail.

sentences.zh: 縱陛下親之愛之，莫若安之福之。

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty personally loves and cherishes them, none is better than securing them and blessing them.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly love them, the greatest kindness is to secure their safety and true welfare.

sentences.zh: 寵祿之過，罪之漸也，非安之也；

translations.literal: Excessive favor and emolument are the gradual onset of guilt—not securing them;
translations.idiomatic: Overindulgence in rank and stipend is the first step toward ruin—not security;

sentences.zh: 驕奢之淫，危之本也，非福之也。

translations.literal: the flood of arrogance and extravagance is the root of peril—not blessing them.
translations.idiomatic: unchecked pride and luxury are the root of calamity—not fortune.

sentences.zh: 前事不忘，後之師也，伏願陛下精求俊哲，朝夕納誨。

translations.literal: Not forgetting past affairs is a teacher for what follows; your servant respectfully wishes Your Majesty to diligently seek the outstanding and wise and morning and evening receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Remember the past—it is your teacher. Seek out the wise and listen to counsel every day.

sentences.zh: 縱有逆於耳、謬於心者，無速之罰，姑籌之以道，省於厥躬。

translations.literal: Even if there is what is contrary to the ear or mistaken in the heart, impose no swift punishment; for the moment consider it through the Way and reflect upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: When counsel wounds the ear or seems wrong, do not punish in haste—weigh it by principle and examine yourself.

sentences.zh: 雖木朴忌忤，願恕之以直，開諫諍之路也。

translations.literal: Though plain and wooden and hateful of opposition, I wish to forgive them for their straightness and open the path of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: However blunt and awkward the speaker, forgive his honesty and keep open the road of frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 或有順於耳、便於身者，無急之賞，當求諸非道，稽之典訓。

translations.literal: If there is what is pleasing to the ear and convenient for the person, grant no hasty reward; one should seek whether it departs from the Way and consult the canonical teachings.
translations.idiomatic: When flattery pleases the ear and suits your convenience, do not reward in haste—investigate whether it accords with principle and with precedent.

sentences.zh: 其不協於德，必置之以法，用杜側媚之行也。

translations.literal: What does not accord with virtue must certainly be settled by law, to block the conduct of lateral flattery.
translations.idiomatic: What fails the test of virtue must be punished by law, to cut off sycophantic intrigue.

sentences.zh: 有羞淫巧於陛下者，遽黜之，則淫巧息矣；

translations.literal: Where someone offers shameful licentious arts before Your Majesty, suddenly dismiss him—then licentious arts will cease;
translations.idiomatic: Remove at once anyone who dares peddle debauchery and trickery before you, and such arts will die out;

sentences.zh: 有進忠讜於陛下者，遽賞之，則忠讜進矣。

translations.literal: where someone offers loyal straightforward counsel before Your Majesty, suddenly reward him—then loyal counsel will advance.
translations.idiomatic: reward at once anyone who speaks loyal and fearless truth, and honest counsel will flourish.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞生於富者驕，生於貴者傲。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that one born in wealth becomes arrogant; one born in honor becomes haughty.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that wealth breeds arrogance and rank breeds pride.

sentences.zh: 石碏曰：「臣聞愛子，教之以義方，不納於邪，驕奢淫逸，所自邪也。」

translations.literal: Shi Que said: "Your servant has heard that to love a son is to teach him the way of righteousness, not to receive him into wickedness. Arrogance, extravagance, dissipation, and idleness—these are the sources of wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Que said: "I have heard that loving a son means teaching him the path of righteousness and keeping him from evil. Pride, excess, dissipation, and idleness are themselves the roots of corruption.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「罔淫於逸，罔游於樂。」

translations.literal: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Do not indulge in idleness; do not wander into pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Do not wallow in idleness; do not lose yourself in pleasure."

sentences.zh: 穆王有命，「實賴前後左右有位之士，繩愆糾謬，格其非心。」

translations.literal: King Mu had a command: "We truly rely on worthy men before and behind, to the left and right, to correct errors and redress mistakes, and to reform wayward hearts."
translations.idiomatic: King Mu commanded: "We depend entirely on worthy men at our side—before and behind, left and right—to correct faults, set errors right, and turn aside unworthy impulses."

sentences.zh: 今儲宮肇建，王府初啟，至於僚友，必惟妙擇。

translations.literal: Now that the Heir Apparent's palace is newly established and the princely households are first opened, as for their staff and companions, they must be chosen with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the crown prince's household is newly established and the princely estates are first opened, every aide and companion must be chosen with the greatest care.

sentences.zh: 今驕奢之後，流波未變；

translations.literal: After generations of arrogance and extravagance, the ripples have not yet stilled;
translations.idiomatic: After years of pride and excess, the tide has not yet fully receded;

sentences.zh: 慢游之樂，餘風或存。

translations.literal: the pleasures of idle wandering may still linger in the wind.
translations.idiomatic: the taste for idle pleasure may still linger.

sentences.zh: 夫小人幸臣，易合於意；

translations.literal: Petty men and favored sycophants easily accord with one's wishes;
translations.idiomatic: Petty flatterers easily tell one what one wants to hear;

sentences.zh: 奇伎淫巧，多適於心。

translations.literal: strange arts and licentious crafts often suit the heart's desires.
translations.idiomatic: exotic tricks and decadent amusements often strike exactly the right note.

sentences.zh: 臣恐狎於非德，茲為愈怠。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that through familiarity with unworthy conduct, he will only grow more indolent.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that through constant exposure to unworthy ways, he will only grow more lax.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「慎簡乃僚，無以巧言令色，其惟吉士。

translations.literal: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Carefully select your staff; do not use those with clever words and pleasing looks—only good men.
translations.idiomatic: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Choose your attendants with care. Do not take men of clever speech and ingratiating manner—only men of virtue.

sentences.zh: 僕臣正，厥後克正；

translations.literal: If the attendants are upright, their lord can be upright;
translations.idiomatic: If attendants are upright, their master can be upright;

sentences.zh: 僕臣諛，厥後自聖。」

translations.literal: if the attendants flatter, their lord will deem himself sage.
translations.idiomatic: if attendants flatter, their master will fancy himself beyond reproach.

sentences.zh: 伏願采溫良博聞之士，恭儉忠鯁之人，任以東宮及諸王府官，仍請東宮量署拾遺補闕之職。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully asks that gentle, learned, and widely informed gentlemen, men who are reverent, frugal, loyal, and bluntly honest, be appointed to offices in the Eastern Palace and in the various princely households, and that the Eastern Palace be permitted to establish posts for remonstrance and filling gaps in governance.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that gentle, learned, and well-informed men—reverent, frugal, loyal, and fearless in speech—be appointed to offices in the crown prince's household and the princely establishments, and that the Eastern Palace be allowed to establish posts for remonstrance and correction.

sentences.zh: 令朝夕講論，出入時從，授以訓誥，交修不迨。

translations.literal: Let them lecture morning and evening, accompany him in going out and coming in, impart instruction and admonition, and mutually cultivate discipline without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Let them instruct him morning and evening, accompany him whenever he goes abroad, teach him by precept and example, and keep one another to the work without slackening.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞馳騁畋獵，令人發狂。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that galloping about in the hunt drives men to madness.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that reckless riding and hunting can drive a man to frenzy.

sentences.zh: 名教之中，自有樂地。

translations.literal: Within the teaching of propriety and moral culture, there is pleasure of its own.
translations.idiomatic: Within the bounds of ritual and moral teaching, there is joy enough.

sentences.zh: 承前貴戚，鮮克由禮。

translations.literal: Following upon former noble kin, few could abide by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Among the noble kin of recent times, few have kept to the rites.

sentences.zh: 或打球擊鼓，比周伎術；

translations.literal: Some played ball and beat drums, vying in skills and arts;
translations.idiomatic: Some played ball games and beat drums, competing in feats of skill;

sentences.zh: 或飛鷹奔犬，盤遊藪澤。

translations.literal: some flew hawks and ran dogs, roaming through marshes and wastes.
translations.idiomatic: others flew hawks and ran hounds, roaming through marshes and wilds.

sentences.zh: 此甚為不道，非進德修業之本也。

translations.literal: This is wholly improper—not the foundation for advancing virtue and cultivating accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: This is deeply unworthy—not the way to build virtue and cultivate character.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「內作色荒，外作禽荒。」

translations.literal: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Within, indulging in the excess of pleasure; without, indulging in the excess of hunting.
translations.idiomatic: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Within, he debauches himself with pleasure; without, he debauches himself with the chase.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「無若丹硃傲，惟慢游是好。

translations.literal: It further says: "Be not like Dan Zhu the arrogant, who loved only idle wandering.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Do not be like arrogant Dan Zhu, who cared for nothing but idle roaming.

sentences.zh: 朋淫於家，用殄厥世。」

translations.literal: Fellow debauchery at home—and so destroyed his line."
translations.idiomatic: He led his household into debauchery together—and so destroyed his house."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下誕降謀訓，敦勤學業，示之以好惡，陳之以成敗，以義制事，以禮制心，圖之於未萌，慮之於未有，則福祿長享，與國並休矣。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers that if Your Majesty, born with counsel and instruction, earnestly applies yourself to learning, shows him what to love and hate, sets forth success and failure, governs affairs with righteousness and the heart with ritual, plans before things sprout and reflects before things exist—then blessings and emoluments will be long enjoyed, and you will share prosperity with the state.
translations.idiomatic: Born to counsel and instruction, Your Majesty should apply yourself earnestly to learning: show him what to love and what to hate, teach him success and failure, govern conduct by righteousness and the heart by ritual, plan before trouble sprouts and reflect before danger appears—then blessings will endure and you will share the realm's prosperity.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞富不與驕期而驕自至，驕不與罪期而罪自至，罪不與死期而死自至。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard: wealth does not appoint a time for arrogance, yet arrogance comes of itself; arrogance does not appoint a time for guilt, yet guilt comes of itself; guilt does not appoint a time for death, yet death comes of itself.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that wealth does not set a date for pride, yet pride arrives unbidden; pride does not set a date for guilt, yet guilt follows on its own; guilt does not set a date for death, yet death comes of itself.

sentences.zh: 信矣斯語，明哉至誡！

translations.literal: How true these words—how clear this supreme warning!
translations.idiomatic: How true these words are—and how clear a warning they offer!

sentences.zh: 頃韋庶人、安樂公主、武延秀等可謂貴矣，可謂寵矣，權侔人主，威震天下。

translations.literal: Recently Wei the Commoner, Princess Anle, Wu Yanxiu, and others could be called noble, could be called favored—their power rivaled the sovereign's, their might shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Consort Wei, Princess Anle, Wu Yanxiu, and their like were as noble as anyone could be, as favored as anyone could wish—their power rivaled the throne, their might shook the empire.

sentences.zh: 然怙侈滅德，神怒人棄。

translations.literal: Yet relying on extravagance, they extinguished virtue—heaven raged and men abandoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet trusting in excess, they destroyed their own virtue—heaven turned against them and men cast them off.

sentences.zh: 豈不謂愛之太極，富之太多，不節之以禮，不防之以法，終轉吉為凶，變福為禍。

translations.literal: Is it not because they were loved to excess and enriched too greatly, unrestrained by ritual, unguarded by law—that in the end good turned to ill and fortune to calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not because they were loved beyond measure and enriched beyond need, unrestrained by ritual and unguarded by law, that fortune at last became disaster and blessing became ruin?

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「千人所指，無病自死。」

translations.literal: A proverb says: "When a thousand men point at you, though there be no illness, you die.
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says: "When a thousand fingers point at you, you die though no wound be found.

sentences.zh: 不其然歟？

translations.literal: Is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: Is that not exactly so?

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「殷鑑不遠，在彼夏王。」

translations.literal: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Yin's mirror is not far—it is in that Xia king.
translations.idiomatic: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Yin's warning is not far off—it lies in that king of Xia.

sentences.zh: 今陛下何勸，豈非皇祖謀訓之則也？

translations.literal: What now should Your Majesty take as encouragement—is it not the counsel and instruction of the imperial ancestor?
translations.idiomatic: What should Your Majesty take as encouragement now, if not the counsel and instruction of the imperial forebear?

sentences.zh: 今陛下何懲，豈非孝和寵任之甚也？

translations.literal: What should Your Majesty take as warning—is it not the excessive favor Emperor Xiaohé bestowed?
translations.idiomatic: What should Your Majesty take as warning, if not the excessive favor shown in the Xiaohé reign?

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「愛而知其惡，憎而知其善。」

translations.literal: 《Book of Rites》 says: "Love yet know their faults; hate yet know their virtues.
translations.idiomatic: 《Book of Rites》 says: "Love them, yet know their faults; dislike them, yet know their virtues.

sentences.zh: 可不慎哉！

translations.literal: Should one not be careful!
translations.idiomatic: Can one fail to be careful!

sentences.zh: 夫寵愛之心則不免，去其太甚，閒之禮節，適則可矣。

translations.literal: The heart that favors and loves cannot be avoided entirely—remove the excess, interpose ritual propriety, and moderation will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Affection itself cannot be denied—but remove what is excessive, set ritual in between, and moderation will do.

sentences.zh: 今諸王、公主、駙馬，亦陛下之所親愛也。

translations.literal: Now the princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law are also those Your Majesty holds dear.
translations.idiomatic: The princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law are also among those Your Majesty loves.

sentences.zh: 矯枉之道，在於厥初，鑑誡之義，其取不遠。

translations.literal: The way to straighten what is bent lies at the beginning; the meaning of taking warning is close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The way to set a crooked course straight lies at the very start; the lesson to be drawn from warning is near at hand.

sentences.zh: 使觀過務善，居寵思危，庶夙夜惟寅，聿修厥德。

translations.literal: Let them observe faults and strive for goodness, hold favor yet think of peril—then perhaps morning and night they will be reverent and constantly cultivate their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Let them study others' faults and strive for goodness, hold favor yet think of danger—then perhaps day and night they will be reverent and ever cultivate their virtue.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「在上不驕，高而不危，所以長守貴也；

translations.literal: 《Classic of Filial Piety》 says: "The superior man does not grow arrogant; though exalted, he is not endangered—thus he long preserves his nobility;
translations.idiomatic: 《Classic of Filial Piety》 says: "He who holds high rank does not grow proud; though elevated, he is not imperiled—thus he long preserves his station;

sentences.zh: 制節謹度，滿而不溢，所以長守富也。

translations.literal: he restrains measure and is careful of bounds, full yet not overflowing—thus he long preserves his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: he restrains himself and keeps within bounds, full yet never overflowing—thus he long preserves his wealth.

sentences.zh: 富貴不離其身，然後能保其社稷。」

translations.literal: When wealth and nobility do not leave his person, only then can he preserve his state and altars.
translations.idiomatic: Only when wealth and rank remain with him can he preserve his house and state.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「制於官刑，警於有位。

translations.literal: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Formulated from official punishments, as a warning to those in office.
translations.idiomatic: 《Book of Documents》 says: "Take warning from the punishments ordained for officials—let those in office be warned.

sentences.zh: 敢有常舞於宮，酣歌於室，時謂巫風；

translations.literal: Those who dare constantly dance in the palace and sing drunkenly in the chamber—this is called the shamanistic wind;
translations.idiomatic: Those who dare dance constantly in the palace and sing drunkenly in their chambers—this is called the shaman wind;

sentences.zh: 敢有徇於貨色，常於游畋，時謂淫風；

translations.literal: those who dare pursue goods and beauty, constantly roaming in hunting—this is called the licentious wind;
translations.idiomatic: those who dare pursue wealth and pleasure, constantly roaming in the hunt—this is called the licentious wind;

sentences.zh: 敢有侮聖言，逆忠直，遠耆德，比頑童，時謂亂風。

translations.literal: those who dare insult the sage's words, oppose the loyal and upright, keep far from elder virtue, and associate with vicious youths—this is called the chaotic wind.
translations.idiomatic: those who dare scorn the sage's words, oppose the loyal and upright, keep away from worthy elders, and consort with vicious youths—this is called the wind of disorder.

sentences.zh: 惟茲三風十愆，卿士有一於身，家必喪；

translations.literal: Of these three winds and ten faults—if ministers and grandees have any one in their person, their house will surely perish;
translations.idiomatic: Of these three winds and ten offenses—if a minister or grandee harbors even one in himself, his house will perish;

sentences.zh: 邦君有一於身，國必亡。」

translations.literal: if a lord of a state has any one in his person, his country will surely perish."
translations.idiomatic: if a ruler harbors even one in himself, his state will fall."

sentences.zh: 甚可畏也，甚可懼也！

translations.literal: How greatly to be feared! How greatly to be dreaded!
translations.idiomatic: How terrifying this is—how dreadful!

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下必察而明之，必信而勸之。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully asks that Your Majesty surely examine and clarify this, surely believe and encourage it.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to see this clearly, believe it firmly, and act upon it.

sentences.zh: 有奢僭驕怠者，削其祿封；

translations.literal: Those given to extravagance, presumption, arrogance, and negligence—strip their stipends and fiefs;
translations.idiomatic: Those guilty of excess, presumption, pride, or sloth—cut their stipends and fiefs;

sentences.zh: 樸素修業者，錫以紳服。

translations.literal: those who are plain, frugal, and cultivate accomplishment—bestow upon them ceremonial sashes and robes.
translations.idiomatic: those who are plain, frugal, and devoted to self-cultivation—reward them with ceremonial honors.

sentences.zh: 以勖其非心，使其奉命，無使久而忽之，無使遠而墜之。

translations.literal: Thus admonish wayward hearts and make them obey commands—do not let it be neglected through long time, do not let it fall away through distance.
translations.idiomatic: Thus warn wayward hearts and keep them to their duty—do not let the effort lapse with time, nor let it fade through neglect.

sentences.zh: 臣聞非知之艱，行之惟艱。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: knowing is not difficult—acting is what is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that knowing is not the hard part—doing is.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「常厥德，保厥位，厥德匪常，九有以亡。」

translations.literal: It is further said: "Constant in his virtue, he preserves his position; if his virtue is not constant, the nine domains will perish.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said: "Keep your virtue constant and you keep your place; let your virtue waver and the realm will be lost.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下慎之哉！

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully asks Your Majesty to be careful!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed this!

sentences.zh: 前車之覆，實惟明證；

translations.literal: The overturned chariot ahead is a clear proof;
translations.idiomatic: The wrecked chariot ahead is proof enough;

sentences.zh: 先王之誡，可以終吉。

translations.literal: the warnings of former kings can bring good fortune to the end.
translations.idiomatic: the warnings of former kings can bring lasting good fortune.

sentences.zh: 若陛下奉伊尹之訓，崇傅說之命，不作無益，不啟私門，刑不差，賞不濫，則惟德是輔，惟人之懷，天祿永終，景福是集。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows Yi Yin's instruction, honors Fu Yue's command, makes nothing without benefit, opens no private gates, never errs in punishment or overflows in reward—then only virtue will be your support, only the people's hearts your refuge; heaven's emolument will end only with your days, and splendid blessings will gather upon you.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty heeds the teaching of Yi Yin, honors the charge of Fu Yue, undertakes nothing useless, opens no door to private favor, never errs in punishment nor overflows in reward—then virtue alone will be your aid and the people's hearts your refuge; heaven's blessings will endure to the end, and great fortune will gather upon you.

sentences.zh: 儻陛下忘精一之德，開恩幸之門，爵賞有差，刑罰不當，則忠臣正士，亦不復談矣。

translations.literal: But if Your Majesty forgets the virtue of singleness of purpose, opens the gate of favor and partiality, makes rank and reward uneven and punishments improper—then loyal ministers and upright men will speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: But if Your Majesty forgets the virtue of single-minded integrity, opens the door to favoritism, makes rank and reward uneven and punishments unjust—then loyal ministers and upright men will fall silent.

sentences.zh: 睿宗覽而善之，令中書省重詳議，擢拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong read it and approved, ordered the Secretariat to reconsider it in detail, and promoted him to appointee as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong read the memorial and approved it, ordered the Secretariat to review it further, and promoted Liu Ze to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era, he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, he rose in succession to Right Vice Director of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 出為鄭州刺史，未行病卒，贈兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Zhengzhou, but before departing he died of illness; posthumously awarded Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Zhengzhou, but fell ill and died before taking up the post; he was posthumously made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 崔義玄

translations.literal: Cui Yixuan
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yixuan

sentences.zh: 崔義玄，貝州武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Yixuan was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yixuan was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業末，往依李密，初不見用。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, he went to serve Li Mi but at first was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he went to join Li Mi, but at first found no employment.

sentences.zh: 義玄見群鼠渡洛，又槊刃有花文，謂所親曰：「此王敦敗亡之兆也。」

translations.literal: Yixuan saw a swarm of rats crossing the Luo, and the blade of his spear bore patterned markings; he said to those close to him: "These are omens of Wang Shichong's defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan saw a swarm of rats cross the Luo River, and noticed patterned markings on his spear blade; he told those close to him: "These are signs that Wang Shichong will fall.

sentences.zh: 時黃君漢守據柏崖，義玄往說之曰：「見機而作，不俟終日。

translations.literal: At that time Huang Junhan held and guarded Baiya; Yixuan went to persuade him, saying: "When you see the moment, act—do not wait for the end of the day.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huang Junhan held Baiya; Yixuan went to persuade him, saying: "When you see your opening, act—do not wait until the day is done.

sentences.zh: 今群盜蜂起，九州幅裂，神器所歸，必在有德。

translations.literal: Now bandits swarm forth like bees; the nine provinces are torn asunder; the sacred vessel will fall to whoever possesses virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarm like bees; the realm is torn apart; the Mandate will fall to whoever holds virtue.

sentences.zh: 唐公據有秦京，名應符籙，此真主也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang holds the Qin capital; his name accords with the celestial tally—he is the true sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang holds the Qin capital; his name matches the celestial portents—he is the true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 足下孤城獨立，宜遵寇恂、竇融之策，及時歸誠，以取封侯也。」

translations.literal: You hold an isolated city alone—you should follow the strategy of Kou Xun and Dou Rong, timely submit in loyalty, and win enfeoffment as marquis."
translations.idiomatic: You hold a lone city in isolation—you should follow the example of Kou Xun and Dou Rong, submit in good time, and win a marquisate."

sentences.zh: 君漢然之，即與義玄歸國。

translations.literal: Junhan agreed, and at once returned to the Tang with Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Junhan agreed, and at once submitted to the Tang together with Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 拜懷州總管府司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Administrator of the Huaizhou Commandery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Administrator of the Huaizhou commandery headquarters.

sentences.zh: 世充遣將高毗侵掠河內，義玄擊敗之，多下城堡。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong sent the general Gao Pi to raid Henei; Yixuan defeated him and captured many fortress-castles.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent the general Gao Pi to raid Henei; Yixuan defeated him and captured many fortified towns.

sentences.zh: 君漢將分子女金帛與之，義玄皆拒而不受，以功封清丘縣公。

translations.literal: Junhan was about to share out women, children, gold, and silk with him; Yixuan refused them all and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qingqiu for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Junhan was about to divide the captives, gold, and silk with him, but Yixuan refused everything; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qingqiu.

sentences.zh: 後從太宗討世充，屢獻籌策，太宗頗納用之。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Taizong in attacking Shichong, repeatedly offering strategies, which Taizong largely accepted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Taizong in the campaign against Shichong, repeatedly offering strategic counsel, much of which Taizong accepted.

sentences.zh: 東都平，轉隰州都督府長史。
