translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Xizhou Regional Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was transferred to chief administrator of the Xizhou regional headquarters.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷左司郎中，兼韓王府長史，行州府事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he served successively as Director in the Left Department of the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently Chief Administrator of the Prince of Han's household, acting on prefectural and commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenguan era he served as Director in the Left Department of the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently as chief administrator of the Prince of Han's household, handling prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 與友人孟神慶雖志好不同，各以介直匡正府幕，王並委任之。

translations.literal: Though he and his friend Meng Shenqing differed in temperament and interests, each by his integrity and bluntness corrected the princely establishment, and the prince entrusted them both.
translations.idiomatic: He and his friend Meng Shenqing differed in temperament and tastes, yet each by his upright bluntness kept the princely household in order, and the prince entrusted them both.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，累遷婺州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, he was promoted in succession to Prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yonghui era he rose in succession to Prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬睦州女子陳碩真舉兵反，遣其黨童文寶領徒四千人掩襲婺州。

translations.literal: When the woman Chen Shuozhen of Muzhou raised troops in rebellion, she sent her follower Tong Wenbao to lead four thousand men in a surprise attack on Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shuozhen, a woman of Muzhou, raised troops in rebellion, she sent her follower Tong Wenbao with four thousand men to strike Wuzhou by surprise.

sentences.zh: 義玄將督軍拒戰，時百姓訛言碩真嘗升天，犯其兵馬者無不滅門，眾皆兇懼。

translations.literal: As Yixuan was about to lead the army to resist, the people were spreading rumors that Shuozhen had ascended to heaven and that anyone who crossed her army would suffer entire clans wiped out—everyone was terrified.
translations.idiomatic: As Yixuan prepared to lead the army out to fight, the people were spreading rumors that Shuozhen had ascended to heaven and that anyone who crossed her forces would see his whole clan destroyed—the troops were terrified.

sentences.zh: 司功參軍崔玄籍言於義玄曰：「起兵仗順，猶且不成，此乃妖誑，豈能得久？」

translations.literal: Assistant For Merit Evaluator Cui Xuanji said to Yixuan: "Armies raised in the name of righteousness sometimes fail even so—this is sorcerer's deceit; how can it long endure?
translations.idiomatic: Merit Evaluator Cui Xuanji said to Yixuan: "Even armies raised in a just cause sometimes fail—this is nothing but sorcerer's trickery. How can it last?

sentences.zh: 義玄以為然，因命玄籍為先鋒，義玄率兵繼進，至下淮戌，擒其間諜二十餘人。

translations.literal: Yixuan agreed, and therefore appointed Xuanji as vanguard; Yixuan led the army after him. Reaching Xiahuai garrison, they captured more than twenty spies.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan agreed, appointed Xuanji as vanguard, and led the main force after him; reaching Xiahuai garrison, they captured more than twenty rebel spies.

sentences.zh: 夜有流星墜賊營，義玄曰：「此賊滅之征也。」

translations.literal: That night a shooting star fell into the rebels' camp; Yixuan said: "This is a sign that the rebels will be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: That night a shooting star fell into the rebel camp; Yixuan said: "This is a sign the rebels will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 詰朝進擊，身先士卒，左右以盾蔽箭，義玄曰：「刺史尚欲避箭，誰肯致死？」

translations.literal: At dawn they pressed the attack; he took the lead before the soldiers. Those beside him shielded him with shields from arrows; Yixuan said: "If the prefect himself seeks to dodge arrows, who will be willing to die fighting?"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they pressed the attack; he led from the front. His attendants tried to shield him with their shields; Yixuan said: "If the prefect himself dodges arrows, who will fight to the death?"

sentences.zh: 由是士卒戮力，斬首數百級，余悉許其歸首。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers exerted all their strength, beheading several hundred; the rest were all permitted to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the soldiers fought with all their might, taking several hundred heads; the rest were allowed to surrender.

sentences.zh: 進兵至睦州界，歸降萬計。

translations.literal: Advancing to the border of Muzhou, tens of thousands surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: As the army advanced to the border of Muzhou, tens of thousands came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 及碩真平，義玄以功拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Shuozhen was pacified, Yixuan was appointed Censor-in-Chief for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuozhen was suppressed, Yixuan was made Censor-in-Chief for his merit.

sentences.zh: 義玄少愛章句之學，《五經》大義，先儒所疑及音韻不明者，兼采眾家，皆為解釋，傍引證據，各有條疏。

translations.literal: From youth Yixuan loved textual studies; on the great meanings of the 《Five Classics》, points doubted by earlier scholars and passages where pronunciation was unclear, he gathered many schools and explained them all, citing evidence on every side, each with its own systematic commentary.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yixuan loved philological study; on the great themes of the 《Five Classics》, points earlier scholars had doubted and passages whose pronunciation was unclear, he drew on many schools, explained them all, and cited evidence for each in systematic commentaries.

sentences.zh: 至是，高宗令義玄討論《五經》正義，與諸博士等詳定是非，事竟不就。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Gaozong ordered Yixuan to discuss the Correct Meaning of the 《Five Classics》 and, with the various Erudites, determine right and wrong in detail—but the project was never completed.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Emperor Gaozong ordered Yixuan to compile the Correct Meaning of the 《Five Classics》, working with the court erudites to settle disputed points—but the project was never finished.

sentences.zh: 高宗之立皇后武氏，義玄協贊其謀。

translations.literal: When Gaozong established Empress Wu, Yixuan assisted and supported the scheme.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong elevated Empress Wu, Yixuan helped advance the plan.

sentences.zh: 及長孫無忌等得罪，皆義玄承中旨繩之。

translations.literal: When Zhangsun Wuji and others were condemned, it was Yixuan who, acting on secret imperial orders, prosecuted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangsun Wuji and others fell from favor, it was Yixuan who, carrying out secret imperial orders, prosecuted them.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，出為蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, he was sent out as Prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing he was posted out as Prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年七十一，贈幽州都督，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, at age seventy-one; posthumously awarded Regional Inspector of Youzhou, posthumous name Zhen ("Upright").
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at seventy-one; posthumously made Regional Inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Zhen, "Upright."

sentences.zh: 則天時思其功，重贈揚州大都督，賜其家實封二百戶。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign, remembering his service, she again awarded him Grand Regional Inspector of Yangzhou and granted his family an actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu's reign, remembering his service, she again honored him as Grand Regional Inspector of Yangzhou and granted his family a fief of two hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 子神基襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shenji inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenji inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，為司賓卿、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: During the Changshou era, he served as Director of the Directorate of Banquet for Tributary Delegates and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era he served as Director of the Directorate for Tributary Envoys and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Orchid Terrace—that is, as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 為相月餘，為酷吏所陷，減死配流。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month as chancellor, he was framed by a ruthless official, sentenced to death commuted, and banished to serve penal exile.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month as chancellor, he was framed by a ruthless official, spared from death, and sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 後漸錄用，中宗初，為大理卿。

translations.literal: Later he was gradually recorded for employment; early in Zhongzong's reign he became Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually brought back into service and, early in Zhongzong's reign, was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 神基弟神慶。

translations.literal: Shenji's younger brother Shenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji's younger brother Shenqing.

sentences.zh: 神慶，明經舉，則天時，累遷萊州刺史。

translations.literal: Shenqing passed the Mingjing examination; in Wu Zetian's time he was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqing passed the classics examination and, under Wu Zetian, rose in succession to prefect of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 因入朝，待制於億歲殿，奏事稱旨。

translations.literal: Because he entered court he was retained at Yisui Hall; his memorials on affairs accorded with the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: On coming to court he was kept on staff at Yisui Hall, and his memorials pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 則天以神慶歷職皆有美政，又其父嘗有翊贊之勳，甚賞慰之，擢拜并州長史。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian, because Shenqing in every post had excellent government and his father had once had merit in assisting the throne, greatly rewarded and comforted him and promoted him to chief secretary of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian noted that Shenqing had governed well in every post and that his father had once rendered loyal service to the throne. She rewarded him warmly and appointed him chief secretary of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 因謂曰：「并州，朕之枌榆，又有軍馬，比日簡擇，無如卿者。

translations.literal: Thereupon she said to him: "Bingzhou is my native soil, and it also has armies and horses; in recent selection there is no one like you.
translations.idiomatic: She told him, "Bingzhou is my homeland, and it holds troops and horses. In the recent round of appointments, no one was better suited than you.

sentences.zh: 前後長史，皆從尚書為之，以其委重，所以授卿也。」

translations.literal: Former and later chief secretaries were all drawn from the Ministry of Personnel; because of the weight of the commission, it is therefore conferred on you."
translations.idiomatic: Past chief secretaries have all been drawn from the Ministry of Personnel. Because this post carries such weight, I am giving it to you.

sentences.zh: 因自為按行圖，擇日而遣之。

translations.literal: She thereupon personally made a map for his inspection tour and chose a day to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: She personally drew up a map for his inspection tour and chose an auspicious day to send him on his way.

sentences.zh: 神慶到州，有豪富偽作改錢文敕，文書下州，穀麥踴貴，百姓驚擾。

translations.literal: When Shenqing reached the prefecture, a powerful magnate forged an edict changing the coin inscription; documents were sent down to the prefecture, grain and wheat soared in price, and the people were alarmed and disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenqing arrived, a wealthy local had forged an edict altering the coinage. Official notices reached the prefecture, grain prices shot up, and the populace was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 神慶執奏，以為不便，則天下制褒賞之。

translations.literal: Shenqing memorialized firmly that it was inconvenient; Wu Zetian thereupon issued an edict praising and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqing memorialized that the change was ill-advised. Wu Zetian issued an edict commending and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 先是，并州有東西二城，隔汾水，神慶始築城相接，每歲省防禦兵數千人，邊州甚以為便。

translations.literal: Earlier Bingzhou had eastern and western cities separated by the Fen River; Shenqing first built the cities to connect, each year saving several thousand defense troops — the border prefectures greatly considered it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou had long been divided into eastern and western cities on opposite banks of the Fen River. Shenqing joined them with new construction, saving several thousand garrison troops each year, to the great benefit of the frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 尋而兄神基下獄當死，神慶馳赴都告事，得召見。

translations.literal: Soon his elder brother Shenji was imprisoned and sentenced to death; Shenqing rode posthaste to the capital to report the affair and was granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his brother Shenji was imprisoned and condemned to death. Shenqing rode posthaste to the capital to plead his case and was granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 則天出神基推狀以示之，神慶據狀申理，神基竟得減死，神慶亦緣坐貶授歙州司馬。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian produced Shenji's interrogation record to show him; Shenqing argued the case on the basis of the record; Shenji at last had his death sentence reduced, and Shenqing was also implicated and demoted to secretary of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian showed him Shenji's interrogation record. Shenqing argued the case point by point, and Shenji's sentence was reduced from death. Shenqing himself was implicated and demoted to secretary of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累轉禮部侍郎，數上疏陳時政利害，則天每嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era he was repeatedly transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, memorialized several times on the advantages and harms of current policy, and Wu Zetian each time praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an period he rose to Vice Minister of Rites and repeatedly memorialized on the strengths and failings of current policy. Wu Zetian praised and accepted his counsel each time.

sentences.zh: 轉太子右庶子，賜爵魏縣子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's household and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's household and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 時有突厥使入朝，准儀注，太子合預朝參，先降敕書。

translations.literal: At that time a Türk envoy entered court; according to ritual regulations the Crown Prince should participate in court audience, and an edict was first sent down.
translations.idiomatic: When a Türk envoy came to court, ritual procedure required the Crown Prince to attend the audience, and an edict was issued in advance.

sentences.zh: 神慶上疏曰：「伏以五品已上所以佩龜者，比為別敕徵召，恐有詐妄，內出龜合，然後應命。

translations.literal: Shenqing memorialized: "Your servant considers that the reason officials of the fifth rank and above wear tortoise insignia is that special edicts summon them, fearing fraud; the tortoise tally is issued from within, and only then do they respond to command.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqing memorialized: "Officials of the fifth rank and above wear tortoise insignia because special summons may be fraudulent. The tally is issued from within the palace, and only then may they obey.

sentences.zh: 況太子元良國本，萬方所瞻，古來徵召皆用玉契，此誠重慎之極，防萌之慮。

translations.literal: Moreover the Crown Prince is the state's foundation, gazed upon by all regions; from antiquity summons have all used jade tallies — this is truly the utmost in weighty caution, the consideration of preventing what is nascent.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince is the foundation of the state and the hope of the realm. Since antiquity, summons to the heir have used jade tallies. This is the utmost caution—the prevention of trouble before it sprouts.

sentences.zh: 昨緣突厥使見，太子合預朝參，直有文符下宮，曾不降敕處分。

translations.literal: Yesterday because the Türk envoy was received, the Crown Prince should attend court — there was only a document sent down to the palace, and no edict was ever issued for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, because of the Türk envoy's audience, the Crown Prince was to attend court—but only a routine notice reached the Eastern Palace. No imperial edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 今人稟淳化，內外同心，然古人慮事於未萌之前，所以長無悔吝之咎。

translations.literal: Now people receive pure transformation and inner and outer are of one heart; yet the ancients considered affairs before they sprouted — thereby they long remained without the fault of regret.
translations.idiomatic: The realm today enjoys enlightened rule and unity within and without. Yet the ancients took thought before trouble arose, and so they long remained free of regret.

sentences.zh: 況太子至重，不可不深為誡慎。

translations.literal: Moreover the Crown Prince is supremely weighty and cannot but be deeply warned and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's position is too weighty for anything less than the deepest caution.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚見，太子既與陛下異宮，伏望每召太子，預報來日，非朔望朝參，應須別喚，望降墨敕及玉契。」

translations.literal: In your servant's foolish view, since the Crown Prince already dwells in a separate palace from Your Majesty, I humbly hope that whenever the Crown Prince is summoned, the coming day be announced in advance; apart from audience on the new and full moon, separate summons should require an imperial edict in ink and a jade tally."
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, since the Crown Prince already resides apart from Your Majesty, I ask that each summons announce the day in advance. Apart from the regular new- and full-moon audiences, every special summons should require an edict in the imperial hand and a jade tally.

sentences.zh: 則天甚然之。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian strongly approved.

sentences.zh: 尋令神慶與詹事祝欽明更日於東宮侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon she ordered Shenqing and Household Administrator Zhu Qinming to attend readings at the Eastern Palace on alternate days.
translations.idiomatic: She soon ordered Shenqing and Household Administrator Zhu Qinming to take turns lecturing at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 俄歷司刑、司禮二卿。

translations.literal: Soon he served in succession as Minister of Punishments and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served in succession as Minister of Punishments and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 神慶嘗受詔推張昌宗，而竟寬其罪。

translations.literal: Shenqing once received an edict to investigate Zhang Changzong but in the end leniently treated his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqing had once been ordered to investigate Zhang Changzong but ultimately treated his offense leniently.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，昌宗等伏誅，神慶坐流於欽州。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, Changzong and others were executed; Shenqing was implicated and exiled to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong reign, Changzong and his faction were executed, and Shenqing was exiled to Qinzhou on account of the case.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: Soon he died, aged over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, aged over seventy.

sentences.zh: 明年，敬暉等得罪，緣昌宗被流貶者例皆雪免，贈神慶幽州都督。

translations.literal: The next year Jing Hui and others incurred guilt; those exiled and demoted on account of Changzong were by precedent all cleared and pardoned; Shenqing was posthumously made Regional Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Jing Hui and others fell from power, those exiled on Zhang Changzong's account were pardoned by precedent. Shenqing was posthumously honored as Regional Commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元中，神慶子琳等皆至大官，群從數十人，趨奏省闥。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, Shenqing's son Lin and others all reached high office; several tens of clan members hurried to memorial at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, Shenqing's son Lin and others all rose to high office, and several dozen kinsmen attended court at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 每歲時家宴，組珮輝映，以一榻置笏，重疊於其上。

translations.literal: At each year's seasonal family banquet, official sashes and seals gleamed; one couch was set with memorial tablets piled upon it.
translations.idiomatic: At the family's seasonal gatherings, official regalia glittered, and a couch was piled high with court tablets stacked one upon another.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶間，中外族屬無緦麻之喪，其福履昌盛如此。

translations.literal: Between Kaiyuan and Tianbao, among kinsmen within and without there was no mourning within the five degrees of relationship — such was the flourishing of their fortune and standing.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns, no member of the clan, near or far, wore mourning—such was the scale of their prosperity.

sentences.zh: 東都私第門，琳與弟太子詹事珪、光祿卿瑤，俱列棨戟，時號「三戟崔家」。

translations.literal: At the gate of the private residence in the Eastern Capital, Lin together with his younger brothers Palace Administrator of the Heir Apparent Gui and Minister of Imperial Entertainment Yao all displayed halberd regalia — at the time they were called "the Three-Halberd Cui family."
translations.idiomatic: At the gate of their Eastern Capital mansion, Lin and his brothers Gui, Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent, and Yao, Minister of Imperial Entertainment, all displayed halberd regalia. They were known as "the Three-Halberd Cui family."

sentences.zh: 琳位終太子少保。

translations.literal: Lin's highest post was Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's highest post was Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：周、隋已來，韋氏世有令人，郁為冠族，而安石嗣立，竟大其門。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From Zhou and Sui onward the Wei clan generation after generation produced admirable men, luxuriant as a leading house, and when Anshi succeeded and established, he at last enlarged their gate.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: From the Zhou and Sui dynasties onward, the Wei clan produced admirable men generation after generation and ranked among the foremost families. When Anshi succeeded to the line, he enlarged the house still further.

sentences.zh: 挺恃才傲物，固虧長者之風，賓王報之以不仁，難與議乎君子矣！

translations.literal: Ting relied on talent and was arrogant toward others — truly lacking the manner of an elder; the Guest King repaid him with lack of benevolence — difficult to discuss with a gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: Ting relied on his talents and treated others with arrogance, falling short of the bearing of a true elder. The Guest King repaid him with harshness—hardly conduct fit for a gentleman!

sentences.zh: 議者以堯、舜有溢美，桀、紂有溢惡，蓋以一為凶德，則群惡所歸。

translations.literal: Discussants hold that Yao and Shun have excess praise and Jie and Zhou have excess blame — broadly, once one is made a vicious virtue, then all vices converge upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say that Yao and Shun are overpraised and Jie and Zhou overcondemned. Once a man is branded with a vicious reputation, every evil is laid at his door.

sentences.zh: 楊素父子，傾覆隋祚，醜聲流聞，雖弘禮、弘武之正士，而元亨兄弟，竟以凶族竄逐。

translations.literal: Yang Su father and son overturned the Sui mandate; foul reputation flowed abroad — although Hongli and Hongwu were upright gentlemen, yet the Yuanheng brothers were at last driven off as a vicious clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su and his sons brought down the Sui, and their ill fame spread far. Though Hongli and Hongwu were upright men, the Yuanheng brothers were still expelled as members of a disgraced house.

sentences.zh: 古人守死善道，不無為也。

translations.literal: The ancients held to death in maintaining the good Way — it was not without purpose.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients held to the right path even unto death—and they did not do so in vain.

sentences.zh: 德威奏議，練刑名之要，俾長秋卿，美哉！

translations.literal: Dewei's memorial and deliberation mastered the essentials of penal names — making him Minister of Autumn Justice — how fine!
translations.idiomatic: Dewei's memorials mastered the essentials of penal law and made him fit for the Ministry of Justice—admirable indeed!

sentences.zh: 審禮仁孝，治行可為世范，卒與禍會，悲夫！

translations.literal: Shenli was filial and benevolent; his conduct in government could serve as a model for the age — yet he at last met with calamity. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Shenli was a man of filial devotion whose conduct in office could serve as a model for the age—yet he met disaster in the end. How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 二閻曲學甚工，措思精巧，藝成而下，垂誡宜然。

translations.literal: The two Yans' bent learning was very skilled, their conception exquisitely refined — when art is accomplished yet one remains below, the warning handed down is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The two Yans were masters of their craft, their conceptions exquisitely refined. When skill outruns rank, the warning they left behind is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 柳氏世稱謇諤，奭、澤有正人風彩，忠規獻納，抑有人焉。

translations.literal: The Liu clan generation after generation was called outspoken and blunt; Shi and Ze had the bearing of upright men — loyal remonstrance and offering counsel — indeed there were such men.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu clan was known for blunt honesty across generations. Shi and Ze had the bearing of true gentlemen, offering loyal remonstrance to the throne—men of that stamp were not lacking.

sentences.zh: 義玄附麗武後，神慶寬縱穢臣，弈世纖邪，以至傾敗，宜哉！

translations.literal: Yixuan attached to Wu Hou, Shenqing was lenient and indulgent toward foul ministers — generation after generation of fine wickedness, reaching ruin — fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan clung to Empress Wu, and Shenqing indulged corrupt favorites. Generation after generation of petty vice led at last to ruin—no more than they deserved!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：韋子驕矜，終損功名。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The Wei son was proud and haughty — in the end he damaged his merit and name.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The Wei scion's pride and arrogance cost him his reputation in the end.

sentences.zh: 楊家積惡，宗門擯落。

translations.literal: The Yang house accumulated wickedness; the clan gate was cast out.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang house accumulated wickedness, and its clan was cast out.

sentences.zh: 閻以藝辱，劉以孝愆。

translations.literal: The Yans were shamed by art; the Lius by filial fault.
translations.idiomatic: The Yans were humbled by their craft; the Lius by a lapse in filial duty.

sentences.zh: 二崔能吏，行無取焉。

translations.literal: The two Cuis were capable officials — in conduct there was nothing to approve.
translations.idiomatic: The two Cuis were capable administrators, but in conduct there was little to admire.
